title.zh: 卷一百一十 列傳第三十五 諸夷蕃將
title.en: Volume 110 Biographies 35: Zhu Yi Fan Jiang
title.raw: 卷一百一十 列傳第三十五 諸夷蕃將 Volume 110 Biographies 35: Zhu Yi Fan Jiang

sentences.zh: 史大柰，本西突厥特勒也，與處羅可汗入隋，事煬帝。

translations.literal: Shi Danai was originally a tegin of the Western Turks. He entered Sui together with Qaghan Chuluo and served Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Danai was a Western Turkish prince who entered Sui with Qaghan Chuluo and served under Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 從伐遼，積勞為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liaodong and, for accumulated merit, was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the Liaodong campaign and, for long service, was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後分其部於樓煩。

translations.literal: Later his tribe was allotted lands at Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: His people were later resettled at Loufan.

sentences.zh: 高祖興太原，大柰提其眾隸麾下。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Danai brought his followers to place themselves under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor raised his banner at Taiyuan, Danai led his followers to enlist under him.

sentences.zh: 桑顯和戰飲馬泉，諸軍卻，大柰以勁騎數百背擊顯和，破之，軍遂振。

translations.literal: At Yinquan Spring Sang Xianhe was fighting and the armies fell back; Danai with several hundred crack horsemen struck Xianhe from the rear, defeated him, and the army recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When Sang Xianhe fought at Drink-Horse Spring and the army was driven back, Danai wheeled several hundred picked horsemen behind the enemy, broke Xianhe's line, and the force rallied.

sentences.zh: 授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He received the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從平長安，以多，賞帛五千匹，賜姓史。

translations.literal: In the pacification of Chang'an, for his many deeds he was rewarded with five thousand bolts of silk and granted the surname Shi.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was taken, his numerous merits earned him five thousand bolts of silk and the imperial surname Shi.

sentences.zh: 從秦王平薛舉、王世充、竇建德、劉黑闥，功殊等，積前後賜侍女三、雜彩萬段。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in subduing Xue Ju, Wang Shichong, Dou Jiande, and Liu Heita; his merit surpassed all others, and in the course of these campaigns he was cumulatively given three palace women and ten thousand lengths of variegated brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju, Wang Shichong, Dou Jiande, and Liu Heita, he outstripped every other officer; over these campaigns he was showered with three palace women and ten thousand lengths of brocade.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，擢累右武衛大將軍，檢校豐州都督，封竇國公，食封戶三百。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards, made acting Military Commissioner of Feng Prefecture, enfeoffed as Duke of Dou State, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he rose through successive posts to General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards and acting governor of Fengzhou, was enfeoffed Duke of the State of Dou, and drew three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made General-in-Chief Assisting the State.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous rank General-in-Chief Assisting the State.

sentences.zh: 馮盎馮盎，字明達，高州良德人，本北燕馮弘裔孫。

translations.literal: Feng Ang, styled Mingda, was a native of Liangde in Gaozhou and a descendant of Feng Hong of Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang, whose style name was Mingda, came from Liangde in Gaozhou and was descended from Feng Hong of Northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 弘不能以國下魏，亡奔高麗，遣子業以三百人浮海歸晉。

translations.literal: Hong could not bring his state to submit to Wei and fled to Goguryeo; he sent his son Ye with three hundred men to cross the sea and return to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bend his kingdom to Wei, Hong fled to Goguryeo and sent his son Ye with three hundred followers across the sea to Jin.

sentences.zh: 弘已滅，業留番禺，至孫融，事梁為羅州刺史。

translations.literal: After Hong perished, Ye remained at Panyu; down to his grandson Rong, the family served Liang as prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong's line was destroyed, Ye stayed at Panyu; by his grandson Rong the clan served Liang as prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 子寶，聘越大姓洗氏女為妻，遂為首領，授本郡太守，至盎三世矣。

translations.literal: His son Bao married a daughter of the great Yue surname Xi and thereby became chieftain; he was appointed prefect of his native commandery, and by Ang's time this had continued for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Bao took a wife from the great Yue clan Xi, became the local chieftain, and was made prefect of the commandery—by Ang's day the family had led the region for three generations.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽初，盎為宋康令，潮、成等五州獠叛，盎馳至京師，請討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou in Sui, Ang was magistrate of Songkang; the Liao of Chao, Cheng, and four other prefectures rebelled, and Ang galloped to the capital to request permission to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wen's Renshou era, while Ang was magistrate of Songkang, the Liao of five prefectures including Chao and Cheng rose in revolt; he raced to the capital and asked to lead the campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 文帝詔左僕射楊素與論賊形勢，素奇之，曰：「不意蠻夷中乃生是人！

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered Left Vice Director Yang Su to discuss the rebels' situation with him; Su marveled and said: "I did not expect such a man to be born among the barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had Left Vice Director Yang Su discuss the rebels' disposition with him. Su was astonished and said, "To think such a man could arise among the frontier peoples!"

sentences.zh: 」即詔盎發江、嶺兵擊賊，平之，拜漢陽太守。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Ang to mobilize troops from the Jiang and Ling regions to attack the rebels, pacified them, and appointed him Grand Warden of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Ang to raise troops from the river and Lingnan regions, crushed the rebels, and made him Grand Warden of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 從煬帝伐遼東，遷左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Yang on the Liaodong campaign and was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Yang against Liaodong and was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 隋亡，奔還嶺表，嘯署酋領，有眾五萬。

translations.literal: When Sui fell he fled back to the Lingnan frontier, rallied chieftains by proclamation, and had fifty thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: After Sui collapsed he returned to Lingnan, gathered the tribal chiefs under his banner, and mustered fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 番禺、新興名賊高法澄、洗寶徹等受林士弘節度，殺官吏，盎率兵破之。

translations.literal: The notorious bandits of Panyu and Xinxing, Gao Facheng, Xi Baochi, and others, placed under the command of Lin Shihong, killed officials; Ang led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Notorious outlaws of Panyu and Xinxing—Gao Facheng, Xi Baochi, and others—served under Lin Shihong, murdered officials, and Ang routed them at the head of his army.

sentences.zh: 寶徹兄子曰智臣，復聚兵拒戰，盎進討，兵始合，輒釋胄大呼曰：「若等識我耶？

translations.literal: Baochi's brother's son Zhichen again gathered troops to resist; Ang advanced to attack, and as the armies had just joined battle he cast off his helmet and shouted: "Do you recognize me?"
translations.idiomatic: Baochi's nephew Zhichen rallied another force to fight back. As the armies met, Ang doffed his helmet and cried, "Do you know who I am?"

sentences.zh: 」眾委戈，袒而拜，賊遂潰，擒寶徹、智臣等，遂有番禺、蒼梧、硃崖地，自號總管。

translations.literal: " The crowd cast down their weapons, bared their torsos, and bowed; the rebels then collapsed, and he captured Baochi, Zhichen, and others, thereby holding the lands of Panyu, Cangwu, and Zhuya, and styled himself Chief Steward.
translations.idiomatic: " The men dropped their weapons, bared their chests, and prostrated themselves; the enemy broke and fled. He seized Baochi, Zhichen, and the rest, took Panyu, Cangwu, and Zhuya, and proclaimed himself regional commander.

sentences.zh: 或說盎曰：「隋季崩蕩，海內震騷，唐雖應運，而風教未孚，嶺越無所系屬。

translations.literal: Someone urged Ang, saying: "The Sui season has collapsed in turmoil and the realm is shaken; though Tang has received the Mandate, its civilizing influence is not yet secure, and Ling and Yue have nowhere to attach themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised him: "The Sui order has crumbled and the empire is in uproar. Tang may have Heaven's mandate, but its civilizing sway is not yet settled, and the Lingnan peoples have no lord to follow."

sentences.zh: 公克平二十州，地數千里，名位未正，請南越王號。

translations.literal: You have subdued twenty prefectures and hold territory of several thousand li; your title and rank are not yet settled—please take the title King of Southern Yue."
translations.idiomatic: You have pacified twenty prefectures across thousands of li, yet your title is unsettled. Take the name King of Southern Yue."

sentences.zh: 」盎曰：吾居越五世矣，牧伯惟我一姓，子女玉帛吾有也，人生富貴，如我希矣。

translations.literal: " Ang said: "I have dwelt in Yue for five generations; among the regional lords only my clan remains. Sons and daughters, jade and silk—I already possess them. In human life, how rare is wealth and honor such as mine."
translations.idiomatic: " Ang replied: "My family has ruled Yue for five generations; we alone remain among the great lords of the south. I already have children, jade, and silk. Few men ever enjoy wealth and rank like mine."

sentences.zh: 常恐忝先業，尚自王哉？

translations.literal: I constantly fear disgracing my ancestors' estate—how could I still make myself king?"
translations.idiomatic: I already fear failing my forebears' legacy—how could I crown myself king?"

sentences.zh: 武德五年，始以地降，高祖析為高、羅、春、白、崖、儋、林、振八州，授盎上柱國、高州總管，封越國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude he first submitted his territory; Gaozu divided it into the eight prefectures of Gao, Luo, Chun, Bai, Ya, Dan, Lin, and Zhen, appointed Ang Pillar of State and Chief Steward of Gaozhou, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yue State.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year five he surrendered his lands. The founding emperor carved out eight prefectures—Gao, Luo, Chun, Bai, Ya, Dan, Lin, and Zhen—made Ang Pillar of State and regional commander of Gaozhou, and enfeoffed him Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 拜其子智戴為春州刺史，智彧為東合州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zhidai was appointed Prefect of Chunzhou and Zhiyu Prefect of Donghezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhidai and Zhiyu were made prefects of Chunzhou and Donghezhou respectively.

sentences.zh: 盎徙封耿。

translations.literal: Ang's fief was transferred to Geng.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's enfeoffment was moved to the state of Geng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，或告盎叛，盎舉兵拒境。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan someone reported that Ang was rebelling; Ang raised troops to block the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was accused of rebellion and mobilized his forces along the border.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔右武衛將軍藺暮發江淮甲卒將討之，魏征諫曰：「天下初定，創夷未復，大兵之余，疫癘方作，且王者兵不宜為蠻夷動，勝之不武，不勝為辱。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered General of the Right Martial Guards Lin Mu to mobilize armored troops from the Jiang and Huai regions to attack him; Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "The realm has just been settled, wounds are not yet healed, and after great armies plague is breaking out. Moreover the king's armies ought not to be moved for barbarians—victory would not be martial, defeat would be shame."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered General Lin Mu to march Jiang-Huai troops against him. Wei Zheng objected: "The empire is barely pacified, the people are still recovering, and plague follows on the heels of war. A Son of Heaven should not march his armies for a frontier chieftain—victory would bring no glory, defeat only disgrace."

sentences.zh: 且盎不及未定時略州縣，搖遠夷，今四海已平，尚何事？

translations.literal: Moreover Ang did not seize prefectures and counties while the realm was unsettled or stir distant barbarians; now the four seas are pacified—what could he still want?"
translations.idiomatic: Ang never seized commanderies while the realm was in chaos or stirred distant tribes. With the empire now at peace, what cause could he have?"

sentences.zh: 反未狀，當懷之以德，盎懼，必自來。

translations.literal: The rebellion is not yet proven; he should be won over with virtue. Ang will be afraid and is sure to come of himself."
translations.idiomatic: There is no clear proof of revolt. Win him with kindness—once he grows afraid, he will come in person."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃遣散騎常侍韋叔諧喻盎，盎遣智戴入侍。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon sent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Wei Shuxie to instruct Ang; Ang sent Zhidai to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Regular Attendant Wei Shuxie to reason with him; Ang dispatched Zhidai to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「征一言，賢於十萬眾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zheng's single remark is worth more than a hundred thousand troops."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "One word from Zheng is worth more than a hundred thousand soldiers."

sentences.zh: 」時暮兵已出，欲遂有功，遣副將上盎可擊狀，帝不許，罷之。

translations.literal: " At that time Mu's troops had already marched; wishing to secure merit, he sent a deputy to submit a report that Ang could be attacked, but the emperor did not permit it and recalled the army.
translations.idiomatic: " Mu's army was already in the field. Eager for a victory, he sent a deputy urging an attack, but the emperor refused and ordered the campaign halted.

sentences.zh: 五年，盎來朝，宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ang came to court; banquets and gifts were exceedingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he came to court and was feasted and rewarded with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 俄而羅、竇諸洞獠叛，詔盎率眾二萬為諸軍先鋒。

translations.literal: Soon the Liao of the cave-districts of Luo and Dou rebelled; Ang was ordered to lead twenty thousand men as vanguard of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the cave peoples of Luo and Dou rose in revolt, and he was ordered to lead twenty thousand men as the army's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 賊據險不可攻，盎持弩語左右曰：「矢盡，勝負可知矣。

translations.literal: The rebels held difficult terrain and could not be attacked; Ang took up a crossbow and told those beside him: "When the arrows are spent, victory and defeat will be known."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held impassable ground. Ang raised his crossbow and told his men, "When our bolts are gone, we will know how this fight ends."

sentences.zh: 」發七矢斃七人，賊退走，盎縱兵乘之，斬首千余級。

translations.literal: " He loosed seven bolts and killed seven men; the rebels retreated, Ang unleashed his troops in pursuit, and more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: " He fired seven bolts and dropped seven men. The rebels fled; he drove his troops after them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 帝詔智戴還慰省，賞予不可計，奴婢至萬人。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhidai to return and console him; rewards were beyond counting, and slave women and servants reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhidai back to comfort him with rewards beyond reckoning, including as many as ten thousand servants.

sentences.zh: 盎善為治，閱簿最，擿奸伏，得民歡心。

translations.literal: Ang was skilled in governance: he examined registers and rankings, exposed hidden wrongdoing, and won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Ang governed well—reviewing registers, exposing hidden crimes, and winning the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左驍衛大將軍、荊州都督。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry and Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子三十人，智戴知名，勇而有謀，能撫眾，得士死力，酋師皆樂屬之。

translations.literal: He had thirty sons; Zhidai was renowned—brave and resourceful, able to win over the masses, he gained warriors who would die for him, and all the chieftains were glad to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He had thirty sons. Zhidai was the best known—bold and shrewd, he could rally the people and win men who would die for him; every chieftain was glad to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 嘗隨父至洛陽，統本部銳兵宿衛。

translations.literal: He once followed his father to Luoyang and commanded his tribe's crack troops in palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: He once accompanied his father to Luoyang and led their picked warriors in palace guard service.

sentences.zh: 煬帝弒，引其下逃歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was assassinated, he led his men in flight homeward.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang was murdered, he led his followers home.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊多，嶺嶠路絕，智戴轉戰而前。

translations.literal: Bandits were numerous at the time and the mountain passes of Ling were cut off; Zhidai fought his way forward.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed the region and the Lingnan passes were blocked; Zhidai fought through them step by step.

sentences.zh: 至高源，俚帥脅為謀主，會盎至，智戴得與盎俱去。

translations.literal: Reaching Gaoyuan, a Li chieftain forced him to serve as strategist; when Ang arrived, Zhidai was able to leave together with him.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoyuan a Li chieftain pressed him into service as adviser; when Ang came up, Zhidai rejoined his father and they left together.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，帝勞賜加等，授衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: Later he entered court; the emperor consoled and rewarded him with added honors and appointed him Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He later came to court, was commended with extra gifts, and was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 聞其善兵，指雲問曰：「下有賊，今可擊乎？

translations.literal: Hearing that he was skilled in warfare, the emperor pointed at the clouds and asked: "There are bandits below—can we attack now?"
translations.idiomatic: Learning of his military skill, the emperor pointed at the clouds and asked, "There are rebels down there—should we strike now?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「雲狀如樹，方辰在金，金利木柔，擊之勝。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The clouds are shaped like trees; the present astral mansion is in Metal. Metal overcomes Wood's softness—attack and you will prevail."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "The clouds look like trees, and the hour belongs to Metal. Metal cuts Wood—attack and you will win."

sentences.zh: 」帝奇其對。

translations.literal: " The emperor marveled at his reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was struck by his answer.

sentences.zh: 累遷左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to General of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈洪州都督。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made governor of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 盎族人子猷，以豪俠聞。

translations.literal: Ang's clansman Ziyou was known for bold chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's kinsman Ziyou was famed for his swaggering courage.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，入朝，載金一舸自隨。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he came to court, bringing a boatload of gold with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he visited court with a whole boatload of gold.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，遣御史許瓘視其貲。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong an imperial commissioner, Censor Xu Guan, was sent to inspect his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong the censor Xu Guan was dispatched to examine his holdings.

sentences.zh: 瓘至洞，子猷不出迎，後率子弟數十人，擊銅鼓、蒙排，執瓘而奏其罪。

translations.literal: Guan reached the cave-district; Ziyou did not come out to welcome him, but later led several dozen kinsmen, struck bronze drums and covered shields, seized Guan, and presented charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan reached the district, Ziyou refused to greet him. Later he led dozens of kinsmen, beat bronze drums and raised shields, seized Guan, and accused him of crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝馳遣御史楊璟驗訊。

translations.literal: The emperor swiftly sent Censor Yang Jing to verify and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurriedly sent Censor Yang Jing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 璟至，卑辭以結之，委罪於瓘。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived he used humble words to win him over and laid the blame on Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing arrived, spoke humbly to placate him, and shifted the blame onto Guan.

sentences.zh: 子猷喜，遺金二百兩、銀五百兩。

translations.literal: Ziyou was pleased and presented two hundred taels of gold and five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Ziyou gave him two hundred taels of gold and five hundred of silver.

sentences.zh: 璟不受。

translations.literal: Jing would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing refused the gifts.

sentences.zh: 子猷曰：「君不取此，且留不得歸。

translations.literal: Ziyou said: "If you do not take this, you will not be allowed to leave."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyou said, "If you refuse this, you will not leave alive."

sentences.zh: 」璟受之，還奏其狀，帝命納焉。

translations.literal: " Jing accepted them, returned and reported the matter; the emperor ordered that they be received into the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing took the gifts, reported what had happened, and the emperor ordered them deposited in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾阿史那社爾，突厥處羅可汗之次子。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er was the second son of the Turkish Qaghan Chuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina She'er was the second son of the Türk qaghan Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 年十一，以智勇聞。

translations.literal: At eleven he was famed for wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: By eleven he was already known for wit and bravery.

sentences.zh: 拜拓設，建牙磧北，與頡利子欲谷設分統鐵勒、回紇、仆骨、同羅諸部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Tuo She, established his headquarters north of the desert, and with Elli's son Yugu She jointly ruled the Tiele, Uyghur, Pugu, Tongluo, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Made a Tuo She, he set up his camp north of the desert and, with Elli's son Yugu She, shared command over the Tiele, Uyghur, Pugu, Tongluo, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 處羅卒，哀毀如禮。

translations.literal: When Chuluo died, he mourned and afflicted himself according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuluo died, he observed mourning with full ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 治眾十年，無課斂。

translations.literal: He governed the people for ten years without levying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years he ruled his people without imposing levies.

sentences.zh: 或勸厚賦以自奉，答曰：「部落豐余，於我足矣。

translations.literal: Some urged heavy taxation for his own support; he replied: "The tribes are abundant—enough for me."
translations.idiomatic: When others urged heavy taxes for his own comfort, he said, "The tribes are prosperous—that is enough for me."

sentences.zh: 」故首領鹹愛之。

translations.literal: " Therefore all the chieftains loved him.
translations.idiomatic: " For this every chieftain held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 頡利數用兵，社爾諫，弗納。

translations.literal: Elli frequently waged war; She'er remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Elli waged war again and again; She'er protested, but his counsel was ignored.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，鐵勒、回紇、薛延陀等叛，敗欲谷設於馬獵山，社爾助擊之，弗勝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the Tiele, Uyghur, Xueyantuo, and others rebelled, defeated Yugu She at Malie Mountain, and She'er aided in the counterattack but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year one the Tiele, Uyghur, and Xueyantuo rebelled and routed Yugu She at Malie Mountain. She'er joined the counterattack but was beaten.

sentences.zh: 明年，將余眾西保可汗浮圖城。

translations.literal: The next year he led his remaining followers west to hold Qaghan Fotu City.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he led the survivors west to hold Fotu, the qaghan's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 會頡利滅，西突厥統葉護又死，奚利必咄陸可汗與泥孰爭國，社爾引兵襲之，得其半國，有眾十余萬，乃自號都布可汗。

translations.literal: When Elli was destroyed and the Western Turkish qaghan Tong Yehu also died, Qaghan Xilibi Duolu and Nishu contended for the realm; She'er led troops to strike them, took half the state, had a following of more than a hundred thousand, and styled himself Qaghan Dubu.
translations.idiomatic: Elli fell, the Western Türk qaghan Tong Yehu died, and Xilibi Duolu and Nishu fought for the throne. She'er attacked, seized half the realm, mustered more than a hundred thousand men, and proclaimed himself Qaghan Dubu.

sentences.zh: 謂諸部曰：「始為亂破吾國者，延陀也，今我據西方，而不平延陀，是忘先可汗，非孝也。

translations.literal: He told the tribes: "Those who first rose in rebellion and destroyed our state were the Xueyantuo. Now that I hold the west, if I do not pacify the Xueyantuo I forget the former qaghan—this is not filial."
translations.idiomatic: He told the tribes, "The Xueyantuo were the first to rebel and break our realm. I hold the west now; if I do not subdue them I forget my forebears' qaghan—where is the filial duty in that?"

sentences.zh: 事脫不勝，死無恨。

translations.literal: If the affair should fail and we do not prevail, I will die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, I will die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」酋長皆曰：「我新得西方，須留撫定。

translations.literal: " The chieftains all said: "We have newly gained the west and must remain to pacify and settle it."
translations.idiomatic: " The chiefs all said, "We have only just taken the west; we must stay to secure it."

sentences.zh: 今直棄之，遠擊延陀，延陀未擒，葉護子孫將復吾國。

translations.literal: Now if we abandon it outright and strike the Xueyantuo from afar, before the Xueyantuo are captured the descendants of Yehu will restore our state."
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon it now and march far to fight the Xueyantuo, Yehu's line will reclaim our realm before we ever capture them."

sentences.zh: 」社爾不從，選騎五萬，討延陀磧北，連兵十旬，士苦其久，稍潰去。

translations.literal: " She'er would not listen, selected fifty thousand horsemen, and attacked the Xueyantuo north of the desert; battle continued for a hundred days, the troops wearied of the length, and gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: " She'er refused. He chose fifty thousand horsemen and marched north of the desert against the Xueyantuo. After a hundred days of fighting the men wearied and began to slip away.

sentences.zh: 延陀縱擊，大敗之，乃走保高昌，眾才萬人，又與西突厥不平，由是率眾內屬。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo loosed an attack and routed him utterly; he then fled to hold Gaochang, with a following of only ten thousand. He was again at odds with the Western Turks, and thereby led his people to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo counterattacked and crushed him. He fled to Gaochang with only ten thousand men left. At odds with the Western Turks as well, he led his people to submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 十年入朝，授左驍衛大將軍，處其部於靈州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he entered court, was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and his tribe was settled at Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he came to court, was made General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry, and his tribe was resettled at Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔尚衡陽長公主，為駙馬都尉，典衛屯兵。

translations.literal: He was ordered to marry the Princess of Chang of Hengyang, made Chief Commandant Escorting the Emperor's Carriage, and placed in charge of guard garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the Princess of Chang of Hengyang in marriage, made Chief Commandant Escorting the Emperor's Carriage, and put in charge of the guard encampments.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以交河道行軍總管平高昌，諸將鹹受賞，社爾以未奉詔，秋毫不敢取，見別詔，然後受，又所取皆老弱陳弊。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as Commander on Campaign of the Jiaohe Circuit he pacified Gaochang; all the generals accepted rewards, but She'er, having received no edict, dared not take the slightest thing—only after seeing a separate edict did he accept, and what he took were all the old, weak, worn, and damaged.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen, as commander of the Jiaohe campaign he conquered Gaochang. Other generals took their spoils, but She'er had no edict and would not touch a thing until a separate order arrived—and then he took only the old, weak, and worthless.

sentences.zh: 太宗美其廉，賜高昌寶鈿刀、雜彩千段，詔檢校北門左屯營，封畢國公。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his integrity, bestowed a jeweled Gaochang saber and a thousand lengths of variegated brocade, ordered him to inspect the Left Garrison Camp at the North Gate, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Bi State.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong commended his integrity, gave him a jeweled Gaochang blade and a thousand lengths of brocade, made him inspector of the North Gate Left Garrison, and enfeoffed him Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，中流矢，揠去復戰，所部奮厲，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed the Liaodong campaign, was struck by a flying arrow, plucked it out and fought again; his command fought with fierce spirit and all won merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he took an arrow, pulled it out, and returned to the fight; his men fought with such fury that all earned distinction.

sentences.zh: 還，擢兼鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to concurrent Minister of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he was also made Minister of Guests.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以昆丘道行軍大總管與契爾何力、郭孝恪、楊弘禮、李海岸等五將軍發鐵勒十三部及突厥騎十萬討龜茲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, as Grand Commander on Campaign of the Kunqiu Circuit, together with the five generals Qibi Heli, Guo Xiaoke, Yang Hongli, and Li Hai'an, he mobilized the thirteen Tiele tribes and a hundred thousand Turkish horsemen to attack Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one, as grand commander of the Kunqiu campaign, he joined Qibi Heli, Guo Xiaoke, Yang Hongli, and Li Hai'an in leading the thirteen Tiele tribes and a hundred thousand Türk cavalry against Kucha.

sentences.zh: 師次西突厥，擊處蜜、處月，敗之。

translations.literal: The army halted among the Western Turks, attacked Chumi and Chuyue, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted in Western Türk territory, struck Chumi and Chuyue, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 入自焉耆西，兵出不意，龜茲震恐。

translations.literal: Entering from west of Yanqi, the troops appeared where none expected; Kucha was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: They entered west of Yanqi where no one expected an army; Kucha was struck with terror.

sentences.zh: 進屯磧石，伊州刺史韓威以千騎先進，右驍衛將軍曹繼叔次之。

translations.literal: Advancing to camp at Qishi, Han Wei, Prefect of Yizhou, led a thousand horsemen forward first, followed by General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Cao Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Qishi. Han Wei of Yizhou led a thousand horsemen ahead, with General Cao Jishu of the Right Valiant Cavalry behind.

sentences.zh: 至多褐城，其王率眾五萬拒戰。

translations.literal: Reaching Duohe City, the king led fifty thousand men to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At Duohe City the king met them with fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 威陽卻，王悉兵逐北，威與繼叔合，殊死戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Wei feigned retreat; the king sent all his troops in pursuit northward; Wei joined with Jishu, fought to the death, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei feigned retreat; the king threw his whole army in pursuit. Wei joined Cao Jishu, fought to the death, and shattered the enemy.

sentences.zh: 社爾因拔都城，王輕騎遁。

translations.literal: She'er thereupon stormed the capital; the king fled on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: She'er then took the capital while the king fled on a swift horse.

sentences.zh: 社爾留孝恪守，自率精騎追躡，行六百里。

translations.literal: She'er left Xiaoke to hold the city and himself led crack cavalry in pursuit for six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: She'er left Guo Xiaoke to hold the city and rode after the king with picked cavalry for six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 王據大撥換城，嬰險自固。

translations.literal: The king held Great Bo City, relying on perilous terrain to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: The king barricaded himself in Great Bo City, trusting the rugged terrain.

sentences.zh: 社爾攻凡四十日，入之，擒其王，並下五大城。

translations.literal: She'er attacked for forty days in all, entered it, captured the king, and together reduced five great cities.
translations.idiomatic: She'er besieged it for forty days, broke in, seized the king, and captured five great cities besides.

sentences.zh: 遣左衛郎將權祗甫徇諸酋長，示禍福，降者七十余城，宣諭威信，莫不歡服。

translations.literal: He sent Colonel of the Left Guard Quan Zhifu to tour the chieftains, showing fortune and calamity; more than seventy cities submitted, and proclaiming authority and trust, none failed to rejoice and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Colonel Quan Zhifu among the chiefs to show them reward and ruin; more than seventy cities submitted. His proclamation of Tang authority won universal glad obedience.

sentences.zh: 刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: He carved stone to record his merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a stone monument to his victory and marched home.

sentences.zh: 因說於闐王入朝，王獻馬畜三百餉軍，西突厥、焉耆、安國皆爭犒師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he persuaded the King of Khotan to come to court; the king presented three hundred horses and livestock to supply the army, and the Western Turks, Yanqi, and Anxi all vied to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then persuaded the king of Khotan to visit the court. The king sent three hundred horses and herds as provisions for the army, and the Western Turks, Yanqi, and Anxi all rushed to present gifts to the troops.

sentences.zh: 孝恪之在軍，床帷器用多飾金玉，以遺社爾，社爾不受。

translations.literal: While Xiaoke was in the army, his bedding, curtains, and utensils were largely adorned with gold and jade; he offered them to She'er, and She'er did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In camp, Xiaoke's bedding and furnishings were lavishly trimmed in gold and jade, which he tried to give to She'er, but She'er refused them.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，曰：「二將優劣，不復問人矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and said: "As for which of the two generals is superior or inferior, I need ask no one further.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he said, "I need ask no one else which of the two generals is the better man.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，請以身殉，衛陵寢，高宗不許。

translations.literal: 」When the Emperor died, he requested to follow him in death and guard the tomb precinct; Gaozong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he asked to die in his service and guard the imperial tomb, but Emperor Gaozong refused.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年卒，贈輔國大將軍、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，治冢象蔥山，謚曰元。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he died; posthumously he was made Supporting-the-State Grand General and military governor of Bingzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling, his tomb fashioned in the likeness of Mount Cong, posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Yonghui (655). Posthumously he was made Supporting-the-State grand general and military governor of Bingzhou, buried at Zhaoling, with a tomb built to resemble Mount Cong; his posthumous title was Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子道真，歷左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Daozhen served as Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daozhen rose to grand general of the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，為邏娑道副大總管，與薛仁貴討吐蕃以援吐谷渾，為論欽陵所敗，盡失其兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianheng he was deputy supreme commander on the Luosuo route, and with Xue Rengui campaigned against Tibet to relieve Tuyuhun; he was defeated by Lun Qinling and lost his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianheng era (670) he served as deputy supreme commander on the Luosuo route. Marching with Xue Rengui against Tibet to rescue Tuyuhun, he was routed by Lun Qinling and lost his whole force.

sentences.zh: 詔有司問狀，免死為民。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to investigate the case; he was spared death and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered an inquiry; he was spared execution and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 阿史那忠阿史那忠者，字義節，蘇尼失子也。

translations.literal: Ashina Zhong, styled Yijie, was a son of Sunishi.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Zhong, courtesy name Yijie, was the son of Ashina Sunishi.

sentences.zh: 資清謹。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and careful.

sentences.zh: 以功擢左屯衛將軍，尚宗室女定襄縣主，始詔姓獨著史。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to General of the Left Garrison Guard, married the imperial clanswoman Princess Dingxiang, and for the first time an edict ordered that the surname alone stand in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made general of the Left Garrison Guard and married the imperial clanswoman, Princess Dingxiang. An edict then required that only the surname Ashina appear in the histories.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀慕過人。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his father, his grief and longing surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father, his grief exceeded that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 會立阿史那思摩為突厥可汗，以忠為左賢王。

translations.literal: When Ashina Simo was established as qaghan of the Turks, Zhong was made Left Wise King.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina Simo was installed as Türk qaghan, Zhong was appointed Left Wise King.

sentences.zh: 及出塞，不樂，見使者必泣，請入侍，許焉。

translations.literal: When he went beyond the frontier, he was unhappy; whenever he saw envoys he wept, and begged to enter court service; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Once he crossed the frontier he was miserable; at the sight of any envoy he wept and pleaded to return to palace service, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 封薛國公，擢右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xue and promoted to Grand General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Duke of Xue and promoted to grand general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 宿衛四十八年，無纖隙，人比之金日磾卒，贈鎮軍大將軍，謚曰貞，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He served as palace guard for forty-eight years without the slightest lapse; people compared him to Jin Midi. At his death he was posthumously made Pacifying-the-Army Grand General, posthumous title Zhen, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: For forty-eight years he guarded the palace without a single fault; men likened him to Jin Midi. When he died he was posthumously made pacifying-the-army grand general, given the posthumous name Zhen, and buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 執失思力執失思力，突厥酋長也。

translations.literal: Zhishi Sili was a Turkish chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishi Sili was a Türk chieftain.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，護送隋蕭後入朝，授左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he escorted Empress Xiao of Sui to court and was appointed General of the Left Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan (627–649) he escorted the Sui empress Xiao to the capital and was made general of the Left Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 會頡利敗，太宗令思力諭降渾、斛薩部落，稍親近。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated, Taizong ordered Sili to announce surrender to the Hun and Husai tribes, and they gradually drew near.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's defeat, Taizong sent Sili to persuade the Hun and Husai tribes to submit, and they gradually came closer to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝逐兔苑中，思力諫曰：「陛下為四海父母，乃自輕，臣竊殆之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was chasing rabbits in the park when Sili remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty is parent to all within the four seas, yet you slight yourself—I privately fear for you."
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was hunting rabbits in the park, Sili admonished him: "Your Majesty is father and mother to the realm, yet you risk yourself—I fear for your safety."

sentences.zh: 」帝異其言。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor marveled at his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his words.

sentences.zh: 後復逐鹿，思力脫巾帶固諫，帝為止。

translations.literal: Later, when he was again hunting deer, Sili removed his cap and belt and firmly remonstrated; the Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When he went hunting deer again, Sili took off his cap and belt and pleaded urgently until the emperor gave up the chase.

sentences.zh: 及討遼東，詔思力屯金山道，領突厥扞薛延陀。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Liaodong was launched, an edict ordered Sili to garrison the Jingshan route and lead Turks to resist the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was ordered to hold the Jingshan route and command Türk troops against the Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 延陀兵十萬寇河南，思力示羸，不與確，賊深入至夏州，乃整陣擊敗之，追躡六百里。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Xueyantuo troops raided the region south of the Yellow River; Sili feigned weakness and would not join battle decisively until the bandits had penetrated as far as Xiazhou; then he formed ranks, defeated them, and pursued six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When a hundred thousand Xueyantuo soldiers invaded south of the Yellow River, Sili played weak and refused a pitched battle until they had pushed deep to Xiazhou; he then formed his line, routed them, and chased them six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 會毘伽可汗死，耀兵磧北而歸。

translations.literal: When Qaghan Pijia died, he displayed his army north of the desert and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Qaghan Pijia's death, he paraded his forces north of the desert and marched home.

sentences.zh: 復從江夏王道宗破延陀余眾。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong in defeating the remaining Xueyantuo forces.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Prince Jiangxia, Li Daozong, in crushing the remnants of the Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 與平吐谷渾。

translations.literal: He shared in the pacification of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 詔尚九江公主，拜駙馬都尉，封安國公。

translations.literal: An edict married him to Princess Jiujiang; he was appointed Chief Commandant of Cavalry Escort and enfeoffed as Duke of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was married to Princess Jiujiang, made chief commandant of cavalry escort, and created Duke of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 坐交房遺愛，高宗以其戰多，赦不誅，流巂州。

translations.literal: He was implicated in the Fang Yi'ai affair; Gaozong, because of his many battles, pardoned him from execution and exiled him to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted in the Fang Yi'ai conspiracy, he was spared execution because of his long record in war and exiled to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 主請削封邑偕往。

translations.literal: The princess requested that her fief income be reduced so she might go with him.
translations.idiomatic: The princess asked to forfeit part of her fief so she could accompany him into exile.

sentences.zh: 主前卒。

translations.literal: The princess died before him.
translations.idiomatic: She died before he did.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，以思力為歸州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era he was made prefect of Guizhou; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo (661–663) he was appointed prefect of Guizhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年，復公主封邑，贈思力勝州都督，謚曰景。

translations.literal: In the first year of Linde the princess's fief was restored; Sili was posthumously made military governor of Shengzhou, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In 664 the princess's fief was restored. Sili was posthumously made military governor of Shengzhou, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力契苾何力，鐵勒哥論易勿施莫賀可汗之孫。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli was grandson of Gelun Yiwushi Mohe Qaghan of the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli was a grandson of the Tiele qaghan Gelun Yiwushi Mohe.

sentences.zh: 父葛，隋末為莫賀咄特勒，以地近吐谷渾，隘翾多癘暍，徙去熱海上。

translations.literal: His father Ge, at the end of Sui, was tegin of Moheduo; because their land lay near Tuyuhun, with narrow passes and much pestilence and heatstroke, they moved beyond the Hot Sea.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ge served as tegin of Moheduo in late Sui. Their territory bordered Tuyuhun, where narrow passes bred plague and heatstroke, so the clan migrated beyond the Hot Sea.

sentences.zh: 何力九歲而孤，號大俟利發。

translations.literal: Heli was orphaned at nine and was styled Great Sijifa.
translations.idiomatic: Heli lost his father at nine and took the title Great Sijifa.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，與母率眾千余詣沙州內屬，太宗處其部於甘、涼二州，擢何力左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, with his mother he led more than a thousand followers to Shazhou to submit; Taizong settled the tribe in Gan and Liang prefectures and promoted Heli to General of the Left Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 632 he and his mother led over a thousand followers to Shazhou to submit. Taizong resettled the tribe in Gan and Liang prefectures and made Heli general of the Left Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 九年，與李大亮、薛萬徹、萬均討吐谷渾於赤水川。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, with Li Daliang, Xue Wanche, and Wan Jun he campaigned against Tuyuhun at Chishui River.
translations.idiomatic: In 635 he joined Li Daliang, Xue Wanche, and Xue Wan Jun in campaigning against Tuyuhun on the Chishui River.

sentences.zh: 萬均率騎先進，為賊所包，兄弟皆中創墮馬，步鬥，士死十七八。

translations.literal: Wan Jun led the cavalry forward and was surrounded by the enemy; both brothers were wounded and fell from their horses, fighting on foot, and seven or eight tenths of the men died.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Jun led the cavalry ahead and was surrounded. Both brothers were wounded and thrown from their horses; fighting on foot, they lost seven or eight men in ten.

sentences.zh: 何力馳壯騎，冒圍奮擊，虜披靡去。

translations.literal: Heli galloped with picked horsemen, broke through the encirclement and struck fiercely, and the barbarians scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Heli charged in with picked horsemen, broke the encirclement, and drove the enemy off in rout.

sentences.zh: 是時吐谷渾王伏允在突淪川，何力欲襲之，萬均懲前敗，以為不可。

translations.literal: At that time the Tuyuhun king Fuyun was at Tuling River; Heli wished to strike him, but Wan Jun, mindful of his earlier defeat, held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king Fuyun was then at Tuling River. Heli wanted to attack him, but Wan Jun, chastened by his earlier defeat, said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 何力曰：「賊無城郭，逐薦草美水以為生，不乘其不虞，正恐鳥驚魚駭，後無以窺其巢穴。

translations.literal: Heli said: "The bandits have no walls or towns; they live by following lush grass and sweet water. If we do not seize them unawares, we shall only startle birds and fish—then later there will be no way to spy out their nests."
translations.idiomatic: Heli said, "These enemies have no walled towns; they live by following pasture and water. Unless we catch them off guard, we will only scatter them like startled birds and fish, and never find their lairs again."

sentences.zh: 」乃閱精騎千余，直搗其牙，斬首數千級，獲橐駝、馬、牛、羊二十余萬，俘其妻子，伏允挺身免。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he reviewed more than a thousand picked horsemen and drove straight at their headquarters; several thousand heads were taken, more than two hundred thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep were captured, their wives and children were made prisoners, and Fuyun alone escaped by his own effort.
translations.idiomatic: He then mustered over a thousand elite horsemen and struck straight at the royal camp. They took several thousand heads, seized more than two hundred thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep, captured the king's family, and Fuyun alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 有詔勞軍於大鬥拔谷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the army rewarded at Great Douba Valley.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the army rewarded at Great Douba Valley.

sentences.zh: 萬均恥名出其下，乃排何力，引功自名。

translations.literal: Wan Jun was ashamed that his fame ranked below Heli's; he therefore pushed Heli aside and claimed the merit in his own name.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to rank below Heli, Wan Jun sidelined him and claimed the victory for himself.

sentences.zh: 何力不勝憤，挺刀起，將殺之，諸將勸止。

translations.literal: Heli could not contain his rage; he drew his blade and rose to kill him, but the generals persuaded him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Heli, furious beyond bearing, drew his sword to kill him, but the other generals restrained him.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝責謂其故，何力具言萬均敗狀。

translations.literal: On their return the Emperor rebuked him and asked the reason; Heli fully related Wan Jun's defeats.
translations.idiomatic: After their return the emperor questioned him sharply; Heli gave a full account of Wan Jun's failures.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，將解其官授何力。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and was about to strip Wan Jun of his office and give it to Heli.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and prepared to remove Wan Jun from office and give his post to Heli.

sentences.zh: 何力頓首曰：「以臣而解萬均官，恐四夷聞者，謂陛下重夷輕漢，則誣告益多。

translations.literal: Heli bowed his head and said: "If you remove Wan Jun from office on my account, I fear that when the four barbarians hear of it they will say Your Majesty favors barbarians and slight the Han—then false accusations will only increase.
translations.idiomatic: Heli kowtowed and said, "If you dismiss Wan Jun because of me, the frontier peoples may think you favor barbarians over Han officers, and slander will only multiply.

sentences.zh: 又夷狄無知，謂漢將皆然，非示遠之義。

translations.literal: Moreover the barbarians are ignorant; they will suppose all Han generals are like this—it is not the way to show authority to the distant."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the barbarians are simple; they will think every Han commander behaves this way. That is no way to win distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 」帝重其言，乃止。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor valued his words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor respected his reasoning and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 有詔宿衛北門，檢校屯營事，尚臨洮縣主。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to guard the north gate in rotation, to inspect and oversee encampment affairs, and he married the County Mistress of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as rotating guard at the north gate and to oversee the encampments, and he married the Lintao county mistress.

sentences.zh: 十四年，為蔥山道副大總管，與討高昌，平之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was deputy supreme commander on the Congshan route, joined the campaign against Gaochang, and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In 640 he served as deputy supreme commander on the Congshan route, took part in the conquest of Gaochang, and helped bring it to submission.

sentences.zh: 始，何力母姑臧夫人與弟沙門在涼州，沙門為賀蘭都督。

translations.literal: At the outset Heli's mother, Lady Guzang, and his younger brother Shamen were in Liangzhou; Shamen was military governor of Helan.
translations.idiomatic: Heli's mother, Lady Guzang, and his younger brother Shamen had remained in Liangzhou, where Shamen served as governor of Helan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔何力往視母。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict ordered Heli to go visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 642 an edict allowed Heli to visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 於是薛延陀毘伽可汗方強，契苾諸酋爭附之，乃脅其母、弟使從。

translations.literal: At that time Qaghan Pijia of the Xueyantuo was growing strong; the Qibi chiefs all vied to attach themselves to him, and they coerced Heli's mother and brother to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo qaghan Pijia was then at the height of his power. Qibi chiefs rushed to join him and forced Heli's mother and brother to go along.

sentences.zh: 何力驚謂其下曰：「上於爾有大恩，且遇我厚，何遽反？

translations.literal: Heli said in alarm to his followers: "The sovereign has shown you great favor and has treated me generously—why rebel so hastily?"
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Heli told his men, "The emperor has done you great kindness and treated me generously. How can you turn against him so suddenly?"

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「可敦、都督去矣，尚何顧？

translations.literal: 」They all said: "The khatun and the governor have already gone—what is there left to consider?"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Your mother and brother have already gone. What is left for us to stay for?"

sentences.zh: 」何力曰：「弟往侍足矣，我義許國，不可行。

translations.literal: 」Heli said: "It is enough for my brother to go and attend them; by duty I have pledged myself to the state—I cannot go."
translations.idiomatic: Heli said, "Let my brother go to serve them. I have pledged myself to the state and cannot leave."

sentences.zh: 」眾執之，至毘伽牙下。

translations.literal: 」The crowd seized him and brought him to Pijia's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The men seized him and brought him before Pijia.

sentences.zh: 何力箕踞，拔佩刀東向呼曰：「有唐烈士受辱賊延邪？

translations.literal: Heli sat cross-legged, drew his belt knife, faced east and cried: "Shall a martyr of Tang suffer insult from the Xueyantuo bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Heli sat with legs sprawled, drew his sword, faced east, and shouted, "Shall a loyal soldier of Tang be shamed by Xueyantuo thieves?"

sentences.zh: 天地日月，臨鑒吾誌。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth, sun and moon—bear witness to my resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth, sun and moon—witness my heart!"

sentences.zh: 」即割左耳，誓不屈。

translations.literal: 」He then cut off his left ear, vowing he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: He cut off his left ear, swearing he would never yield.

sentences.zh: 毘伽怒，欲殺之，其妻諫而止。

translations.literal: Pijia was enraged and wished to kill him, but his wife remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Pijia was furious and meant to kill him, but his wife dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 何力被執也，或讒之帝曰：「何力入延陀如涸魚得水，其脫必遽。

translations.literal: When Heli had been seized, some slandered him to the Emperor, saying: "Heli among the Xueyantuo is like a dried fish returned to water—if he escapes, it will be swift."
translations.idiomatic: While Heli was held captive, some told the emperor, "Heli among the Xueyantuo is like a fish back in water. If he gets free, he will desert at once."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不然。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "No.

sentences.zh: 若人心如鐵石，殆不背我。

translations.literal: If his heart is iron and stone, he will hardly betray me."
translations.idiomatic: If his heart is iron, he will hardly turn against me."

sentences.zh: 」會使至言狀，帝泣下。

translations.literal: 」When an envoy arrived and reported the circumstances, the Emperor wept.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy arrived with the full account, the emperor wept.

sentences.zh: 即詔兵部侍郎崔敦禮持節許延陀尚主，因求何力，乃得還。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Vice Minister of War Cui Dunli to bear credentials, promise the Xueyantuo an imperial marriage, and thereby demand Heli's return; only then was Heli recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent Vice Minister of War Cui Dunli with credentials to promise the Xueyantuo an imperial bride and demand Heli back, and Heli was restored.

sentences.zh: 授右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 公主行有日，何力陳不可。

translations.literal: The day for the princess's departure drew near; Heli submitted that it should not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess's departure drew near, Heli urged that the marriage should not go ahead.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天子無戲言，既許之，叵奈何？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Son of Heaven does not speak in jest; having already promised, what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A Son of Heaven does not jest. The promise is given—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 」何力曰：「禮有親迎，宣詔毘伽身到京師，或詣靈武。

translations.literal: 」Heli said: "Rites require the groom to come in person; proclaim that Pijia must come himself to the capital, or at least to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Heli said, "Proper rites require the groom to come in person. Proclaim that Pijia must appear at the capital, or at least at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 彼畏我，必不來，則姻不成，而憂憤不知所出，下必攜貳，不及一年，交相疑沮。

translations.literal: They fear us and will surely not come; then the marriage will not be concluded, yet anxiety and rage will have no outlet, the lower ranks will surely split in loyalty, and within less than a year mutual suspicion and discouragement will set in.
translations.idiomatic: They fear us and will not come. The marriage will fail, yet their frustration will have no outlet. Their followers will turn divided; within a year they will be torn by mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 毘伽素狼戾，必死，死則二子爭國。

translations.literal: Pijia has always been fierce and unruly; he will surely die, and when he dies his two sons will contend for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Pijia is violent by nature; he will die of it. When he dies, his two sons will fight over the khanate.

sentences.zh: 內判外攜，不戰而擒矣。

translations.literal: With strife within and defection without, they can be taken without battle."
translations.idiomatic: With civil strife at home and allies peeling away abroad, we can take them without fighting."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 毘伽果不敢迎，郁邑不得誌，恚而死，少子拔酌殺其庶兄突利失自立，國中亂，如其策雲。

translations.literal: Pijia indeed did not dare come to meet her; Yuyi could not fulfill his aim and died of rage; the younger son Bazhuo killed his half-brother Tuli Shi and set himself up; the realm fell into disorder—just as Heli had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: Pijia indeed dared not come. His eldest son Yuyi, thwarted in his ambition, died of rage. The younger son Bazhuo killed his half-brother Tuli Shi and seized power; the realm fell into chaos, exactly as Heli had foretold.

sentences.zh: 帝征高麗，詔何力為前軍總管。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goryeo, an edict made Heli commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Goryeo campaign the emperor appointed Heli commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 次白崖城，中賊槊，創甚，帝自為傅藥。

translations.literal: Halting at White Cliff City, he was struck by an enemy spear and was badly wounded; the Emperor himself applied medicine.
translations.idiomatic: At White Cliff City he was speared by the enemy and badly wounded; the emperor personally dressed his wound.

sentences.zh: 城拔，得刺何力者高突勃，騶使自殺之，辭曰：「彼為其主，冒白刃以刺臣，此義士也。

translations.literal: When the city was taken, they seized Gaotubo, who had stabbed Heli, and attendants were sent to execute him; Heli declined, saying: "He served his lord and braved bare blades to stab me—this is a man of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell they caught Gaotubo, who had wounded him, and attendants were told to execute him. Heli refused, saying, "He served his lord and faced death to strike me—that is a loyal man."

sentences.zh: 犬馬猶報其養，況於人乎？

translations.literal: Even dogs and horses repay those who rear them—how much more so a man?"
translations.idiomatic: Even dogs and horses repay those who feed them—how much more a man?"

sentences.zh: 」卒舍之。

translations.literal: 」In the end he spared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he let him live.

sentences.zh: 俄以昆丘道總管平龜茲。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, as supreme commander on the Kunqiu route, he pacified Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as supreme commander on the Kunqiu route, he pacified Kucha.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，欲以身殉，高宗諭止。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, he wished to follow him in death; Gaozong admonished him and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he wished to die in his service, but Emperor Gaozong dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，西突厥阿史那賀魯以處月、處蜜、姑蘇、歌邏祿、卑失五姓叛，寇延州，陷金嶺略蒲類，詔何力為弓月道大總管，率左武衛大將軍梁建方，統秦、成、岐、雍及燕然都護回紇兵人萬討之。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era Ashina Helu of the Western Turks led the five surnames Chuyue, Chumi, Gusu, Geluolu, and Bishi in rebellion, raided Yanzhou, seized Jinling and plundered Pulei; an edict made Heli supreme commander on the Gongyue route, leading Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Liang Jianfang to command troops from Qin, Cheng, Qi, Yong, and ten thousand Uighur soldiers of the Yanshan Protectorate against them.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui (650–655) Ashina Helu of the Western Turks rallied the Chuyue, Chumi, Gusu, Qarluq, and Bishi clans in revolt, attacked Yanzhou, and seized Jinling and Pulei. Heli was made supreme commander on the Gongyue route and, with Grand General Liang Jianfang of the Left Martial Guard, led forces from Qin, Cheng, Qi, Yong, and ten thousand Uighur troops of the Yanshan Protectorate against them.

sentences.zh: 處月酋硃邪孤註遂殺招慰使果毅都尉單道惠，據牢山以守。

translations.literal: The Chuyue chief Zhuye Guzhu then killed the pacification envoy Guoyi Colonel Shan Daohui and held Laoshan to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Chuyue chief Zhuye Guzhu killed the pacification envoy, Colonel Shan Daohui, and fortified himself on Laoshan.

sentences.zh: 何力等分兵數道，攀F〗脲而上，急攻之，賊大潰，孤註液遁。

translations.literal: Heli and the others divided their forces along several routes, climbed the heights to assault, pressed the attack hotly, and the rebels were utterly routed; Guzhu fled.
translations.idiomatic: Heli divided his forces along several routes, scaled the heights to attack, and pressed the assault until the enemy broke completely; Guzhu fled.

sentences.zh: 輕騎窮躡，行五百里，孤註戰死。

translations.literal: Light cavalry pursued to the end for five hundred li; Guzhu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Light cavalry pursued him five hundred li; Guzhu was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 虜渠帥六十，俘斬萬余，牛馬雜畜七萬，取處蜜時健俟斤、合支賀等以歸。

translations.literal: Sixty enemy chieftains were taken, more than ten thousand were captured or killed, seventy thousand mixed cattle and livestock were seized, and Shijian Sijin of Chumi, Hezhi He, and others were brought back.
translations.idiomatic: They captured sixty enemy chiefs, killed or took more than ten thousand men, seized seventy thousand head of livestock, and brought back Shijian Sijin of Chumi, Hezhi He, and others.

sentences.zh: 遷左驍衛大將軍，封郕國公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and created Duke of Xing.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，為沮江軍行軍大總管，與蘇定方及右驍衛大將軍劉伯英代高麗。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era he was supreme commander of the Zujiang Army campaign, and with Su Dingfang and Grand General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Liu Boying invaded Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing (656–661) he served as supreme commander of the Zujiang army and, with Su Dingfang and Grand General Liu Boying of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard, campaigned against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: ，不克。

translations.literal: , but they did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: , but they failed to conquer it.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，復拜遼東道行軍大總管，率諸蕃三十五軍進討，帝欲自率師繼之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo he was again appointed supreme commander of the Liaodong route, led thirty-five allied barbarian armies forward in attack, and the Emperor intended to follow in person with his army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longshuo (661) he was again made supreme commander on the Liaodong route, led thirty-five allied frontier armies in the advance, and the emperor planned to follow with the main force.

sentences.zh: 次鴨綠水，蓋蘇文遣男生以精兵數萬拒險，眾莫敢濟。

translations.literal: Halting at the Yalu River, Gaisuwen sent Namsaeng with tens of thousands of picked troops to hold the defiles; none dared cross.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yalu River, Yeon Gaesomun sent his son Namsaeng with tens of thousands of elite troops to block the crossing; no one dared ford the river.

sentences.zh: 會冰合，何力引兵噪而濟，賊驚，遂潰。

translations.literal: When the ice had joined, Heli led his troops across with a clamor; the enemy were startled and thereupon broke.
translations.idiomatic: When the ice froze solid, Heli led his men across with a great shout. The enemy panicked and broke.

sentences.zh: 斬首三萬級，余眾降，男生脫身走。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand heads were taken, the remainder surrendered, and Namsaeng escaped by himself.
translations.idiomatic: They took thirty thousand heads; the rest surrendered, and Namsaeng fled alone.

sentences.zh: 有詔斑師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the army withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 時鐵勒九姓叛，詔何力為安撫大使。

translations.literal: At that time the nine surnames of the Tiele rebelled; an edict made Heli Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine Tiele tribes rebelled, Heli was appointed pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 何力以輕騎五百馳入其部，虜大驚。

translations.literal: Heli with five hundred light horsemen galloped into their encampment; the barbarians were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Heli raced into their camp at the head of five hundred light cavalry, and the tribesmen panicked.

sentences.zh: 何力喻曰：「朝家知而詿誤，遂及翻動，使我貰爾過，得自新。

translations.literal: Heli instructed them, saying: "The court knows you were deceived and mistaken, and thus stirred to revolt; let me bear your offense upon myself, that you may renew yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Heli addressed them: "The throne understands you were misled into error and rose in rebellion. I have come to shoulder your guilt so you may start anew."

sentences.zh: 罪在兇渠，取之則已。

translations.literal: The guilt lies with the violent ringleaders; seize them and that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ringleaders are to blame—hand them over and the matter ends there.

sentences.zh: 」九姓大喜，共擒偽葉護及特勒等二百人以歸，何力數其罪，誅之，余眾遂安。

translations.literal: " The Nine Surnames were greatly pleased; together they seized the false Yehu and Tegin and two hundred others and returned. Heli enumerated their crimes and executed them; the remaining multitude thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Surnames were overjoyed. They seized the false qaghan, the tegins, and two hundred conspirators and brought them in. Heli recited their crimes and put them to death, and the rest of the people were pacified.

sentences.zh: 士卒道死者，令所在收瘞，蠲護其家。

translations.literal: Soldiers who died on the road—he ordered each place to collect and bury them, and remit obligations to protect their families.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his men had died along the march, he ordered the bodies collected and buried and their households relieved of burdens.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蓋蘇文死，男生為弟所逐，使子詣闕請降，乃拜何力為遼東道行軍大總管、安撫大使經略之，副李勣同趨高麗勣已拔新城，留何力守。

translations.literal: Before long Gaisuwen died; Namseng was driven out by his younger brother; he sent his son to the court to request surrender. Thereupon Heli was appointed Grand General of the Liaodong Circuit campaign army and Pacification Commissioner to oversee affairs, assisting Li Jiji in marching on Goguryeo. Jiji had already taken Xincheng and left Heli to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yeon Gaesomun died, and Namseng was ousted by his younger brother. He sent his son to the capital to offer surrender. The court then named Heli Grand General of the Liaodong campaign and Pacification Commissioner, with Li Jiji as his deputy for the advance on Goguryeo. Jiji had already seized Xincheng and left Heli to hold it.

sentences.zh: 時高麗兵十五萬屯遼水，引靺鞨數萬眾據南蘇城，何力奮擊，破之，斬首萬級，乘勝進拔八城。

translations.literal: At the time one hundred fifty thousand Goguryeo troops were stationed at Liaoshui, leading tens of thousands of Mohe to hold Nansu city. Heli struck fiercely, defeated them, took heads in the myriads, and pressing the victory advanced to capture eight cities.
translations.idiomatic: A Goguryeo force of a hundred and fifty thousand held the Liaoshui line, with tens of thousands of Mohe occupying Nansu. Heli attacked with fury, routed them, took ten thousand heads, and pressed on to seize eight cities in succession.

sentences.zh: 引兵還，與勣會合，攻辱夷、大行二城，克之。

translations.literal: He led the army back and joined Jiji; they attacked the two cities of Ruyi and Daxing and took them.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and rejoined Jiji, and together they stormed and captured Ruyi and Daxing.

sentences.zh: 進拔扶余。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward and took Buyeo as well.

sentences.zh: 勣勒兵未進，何力率兵五十萬先趨平壤，勣繼進，攻凡七月，拔之，虜其王以獻。

translations.literal: Jiji held the army from advancing; Heli led five hundred thousand troops first toward Pyongyang; Jiji followed in pursuit. They attacked for fully seven months and took it, capturing the king and presenting him.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiji held his main force back, Heli marched half a million men on Pyongyang ahead of him; Jiji came up afterward. The siege lasted seven months before the city fell. They seized the king and sent him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 進鎮軍大將軍，行左衛大將軍，徙封涼。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army, acting Left Guard General; his fief was shifted to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and served as acting Left Guard General; his enfeoffment was moved to Liang.

sentences.zh: 總章、儀鳳間，吐蕃滅吐谷渾，勢益張，入寇鄯、廓、河、坊等州，詔周王為洮州道、相王為涼州道行軍元帥，率何力等討之。

translations.literal: Between Zongzhang and Yifeng, Tibet destroyed Tuyuhun and its power grew ever greater; it invaded Zheng, Kuo, He, Fang and other prefectures. An edict made the Prince of Zhou campaign marshal of the Taozhou circuit and the Prince of Xiang of the Liangzhou circuit, leading Heli and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zongzhang and Yifeng reigns Tibet destroyed Tuyuhun and grew bolder still, raiding Zheng, Kuo, He, Fang, and neighboring prefectures. The throne ordered the Prince of Zhou and the Prince of Xiang to serve as marshals of the Taozhou and Liangzhou circuits respectively, with Heli among the generals sent against them.

sentences.zh: 二王不行，亦會何力卒。

translations.literal: The two princes did not go; moreover it happened that Heli died.
translations.idiomatic: Neither prince took the field—and before the campaign could go forward, Heli died.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國大將軍、并州大都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰毅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand General Who Assists the State and Governor-General of Bingzhou; he was buried at Zhaoling with posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand General Who Assists the State and Governor-General of Bingzhou, buried at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous name Resolute.

sentences.zh: 始，龍朔中，司稼少卿梁脩仁新作大明宮，植白楊於庭，示何力曰：「此木易成，不數年可庇。

translations.literal: At the beginning—in the Longshuo era—Liang Xiuren, Vice Minister of Agriculture, newly built Daming Palace and planted white poplars in the courtyard, showing Heli and saying: "This tree grows easily; within a few years it can give shade."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Longshuo, Vice Minister of Agriculture Liang Xiuren had just built Daming Palace and set white poplars in the courtyard. He pointed them out to Heli and said, "They grow fast—you'll have shade in just a few years."

sentences.zh: 」何力不答，但誦「白楊多悲風，蕭蕭愁殺人」之句，脩仁驚悟，更植以桐。

translations.literal: " Heli did not answer but recited the lines "White poplars—many mournful winds; rustling, rustling, they slay men's hearts." Xiuren was startled and came to understand; he replanted with paulownia.
translations.idiomatic: Heli said nothing, only reciting: "White poplars know many mournful winds; rustling, rustling, they break the heart." Xiuren took the hint and replaced them with paulownia.

sentences.zh: 子明子明，字若水，孺褓授上柱國，封漁陽縣公。

translations.literal: His son Ming, style name Ruoshui—in swaddling clothes was given the rank Superior Pillar of State and enfeoffed Duke of Yuyang county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ming, courtesy name Ruoshui, was made Superior Pillar of State while still in the cradle and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 年十二，遷奉輦大夫。

translations.literal: At age twelve he was transferred to Palanquin Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was appointed Palanquin Attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 李敬玄征吐蕃，明為柏海道經略使，以戰多，進左威衛大將軍，襲封，賜錦袍、寶帶，它物蕃夥。

translations.literal: When Li Jingxuan campaigned against Tibet, Ming was commissioner of the Bohai circuit; for many battles he was promoted to General of the Left Might Guard, inherited the fief, and was given brocade robes, a treasured belt, and many other things in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: On Li Jingxuan's Tibetan campaign Ming served as commissioner of the Bohai route. After repeated victories he rose to General of the Left Might Guard, inherited his father's title, and received brocade robes, a jeweled belt, and a lavish assortment of other gifts.

sentences.zh: 擢嫡子三品官。

translations.literal: His eldest legitimate son was raised to a third-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son by the principal wife was promoted to the third rank.

sentences.zh: 再遷雞田道大總管，至烏德鞬山，誘附二萬帳。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Grand General of the Jitian circuit; arriving at Wudeqian Mountain he induced two myriad tents to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Grand General of the Jitian circuit and, reaching Wudeqian Mountain, won over twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武後時，明妻及母臨洮縣主皆賜姓武。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, Ming's wife and his mother the Princess of Lintao were both granted the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, both Ming's wife and his mother, the Princess of Lintao, were given the imperial surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 以左鷹揚衛大將軍卒，年四十六，贈涼州刺史，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: He died as General of the Left Hawk-and-Bow Guard, age forty-six; posthumously made Governor of Liangzhou with posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as General of the Left Hawk-and-Bow Guard at forty-six. He was posthumously made Governor of Liangzhou and given the posthumous name Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 明性淹厚，喜學，長辯論。

translations.literal: Ming's nature was deep and generous; he delighted in learning and excelled in disputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ming was thoughtful and magnanimous, devoted to study, and a gifted debater.

sentences.zh: 子聳，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Song inherited the peerage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Song succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 黑齒常之黑齒常之，百濟西部人。

translations.literal: Heichi Changzhi—Heichi Changzhi was a man of western Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Heichi Changzhi was a native of western Baekje.

sentences.zh: 長七尺余，驍毅有謀略。

translations.literal: He stood over seven chi in height, fierce and resolute, with strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than seven feet tall—fearless, resolute, and a shrewd tactician.

sentences.zh: 為百濟達率兼風達郡將，猶唐刺史雲。

translations.literal: He was a dara of Baekje concurrently general of Fengda commandery—like a Tang prefect, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Baekje rank of dara and served also as general of Fengda commandery—roughly the equivalent of a Tang prefect.

sentences.zh: 蘇定方平百濟，常之以所部降。

translations.literal: When Su Dingfang pacified Baekje, Changzhi surrendered with his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Dingfang conquered Baekje, Changzhi submitted with the troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 而定方囚老王，縱兵大掠，常之懼，與左右酋長十余人遁去，嘯合逋亡，依任存山自固，不旬日，歸者三萬。

translations.literal: But Dingfang imprisoned the old king and let his troops plunder greatly; Changzhi was afraid. With over ten chieftains of his close followers he fled, gathered dispersed men, and relying on Mount Ren preserved himself. In less than ten days thirty thousand returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang, however, imprisoned the old king and let his men loot at will. Changzhi fled in alarm with a dozen close chieftains, rallied scattered refugees, and made a stand on Mount Ren. Within ten days thirty thousand men had rejoined him.

sentences.zh: 定方勒兵攻之，不克，常之遂復二百余城。

translations.literal: Dingfang led troops to attack him but could not overcome him; Changzhi thereby recovered over two hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang attacked him in force but failed to break him, and Changzhi went on to recover more than two hundred towns.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，高宗遣使招諭，乃詣劉仁軌降。

translations.literal: In Longshuo Emperor Gaozong sent envoys to summon and instruct him; thereupon he went to Liu Ren'gui and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo the emperor sent envoys to win him over, and Changzhi went to Liu Ren'gui to submit.

sentences.zh: 累遷左領軍員外將軍、洋州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Left Army Outsider General and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to acting Left Army Outsider General and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，從李敬玄、劉審禮擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng he followed Li Jingxuan and Liu Shenli to attack Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng he campaigned against Tibet under Li Jingxuan and Liu Shenli.

sentences.zh: 審禮敗，敬玄欲引還，阻泥溝，兵不得出，賊屯高壓官軍。

translations.literal: Shenli was defeated; Jingxuan wished to withdraw but was blocked at Nigou—the army could not get out; the bandits held the high ground and pressed on the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Shenli was beaten, and as Jingxuan tried to pull back his force was trapped at Nigou and could not break out. The enemy held the heights and bore down on the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 常之夜率敢死士五百人掩其營，殺掠數百人，賊酋跋地設棄軍走。

translations.literal: Changzhi by night led five hundred dare-to-die men to raid their camp; they killed and plundered several hundred; the bandit chief Bodhishe abandoned his army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi led five hundred volunteers in a night assault on the enemy camp, killing and plundering hundreds before the Tibetan chief Bodhishe abandoned his army and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆其才，擢左武衛將軍，檢校左羽林軍，賜金帛殊等。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed at his talent; he was promoted to General of the Left Martial Guard, inspected the Left Forest Army, and was given gold and silk of special grade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at his ability, promoted him to General of the Left Martial Guard with oversight of the Left Forest Army, and rewarded him with gold and silk of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 進為河源軍副使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to be deputy commissioner of Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made deputy commander of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 調露中，吐蕃使贊婆等入寇，屯良非川。

translations.literal: In the Diaolu era the Tibetan envoy Zanpo and others invaded and camped at Liangfei River.
translations.idiomatic: During Diaolu the Tibetan generals Zanpo and others crossed the border and encamped on the Liangfei River.

sentences.zh: 李敬玄之敗，常之引精騎三千夜襲其軍，斬首二千級，獲羊馬數萬，贊婆等單騎去。

translations.literal: After Li Jingxuan's defeat, Changzhi led three thousand elite cavalry by night to raid their army, taking two thousand heads and capturing tens of thousands of sheep and horses; Zanpo and others fled alone on horseback.
