translations.idiomatic: Following Li Jingxuan's rout, Changzhi struck at night with three thousand picked horsemen, taking two thousand heads and tens of thousands of sheep and horses while Zanpo and his officers fled alone.

sentences.zh: 即拜河源道經略大使。

translations.literal: He was forthwith appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Heyuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately named Pacification Commissioner of the Heyuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 因建言河源當賊沖，宜增兵鎮守，而運饟須廣。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted advice that Heyuan faced the bandits' thrust and should have added troops for defense, while transport of provisions must be expanded.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Heyuan lay on the enemy's main axis of attack and needed stronger garrisons, with a far larger supply train.

sentences.zh: 乃斥地置烽七十所，墾田五千頃，歲收粟斛百余萬。

translations.literal: He then cleared land and set up seventy beacon stations, opened five thousand qing of fields, and collected over a million hu of grain yearly.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared frontier land, built seventy beacon towers, opened five thousand qing to the plow, and harvested more than a million hu of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 由是食衍士精，戍邏有備。

translations.literal: From this food was abundant and soldiers keen; border patrol had preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions grew plentiful, the troops stayed sharp, and the frontier patrols were always ready.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，贊婆營青海，常之馳掩其屯，破之，悉燒糧廥，獲羊、馬、甲首不貲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, Zanpo camped at Qinghai; Changzhi galloped to raid his encampment, defeated them, burned all the granaries, and captured sheep, horses, armor and heads beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonglong, Zanpo encamped at Qinghai. Changzhi swept down on the camp, routed the Tibetans, burned their granaries to ash, and took sheep, horses, armor, and heads beyond number.

sentences.zh: 詔書勞賜。

translations.literal: An imperial edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent an edict of commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 凡蒞軍七年，吐蕃檐畏，不敢盜邊。

translations.literal: For seven years in all he commanded the army; Tibet feared him and dared not raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: In seven years of command he so cowed the Tibetans that they no longer dared raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 封燕國公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，突厥復犯塞，常之率兵追擊，至兩井，忽與賊遇，賊騎三千方擐甲，常之見其囂，以二百騎突之，賊皆棄甲去。

translations.literal: In Chuigong the Turks again violated the frontier; Changzhi led troops in pursuit to Liangjing. Suddenly they met the bandits—three thousand bandit horsemen were just donning armor. Changzhi saw their arrogance; with two hundred riders he charged them and the bandits all cast off armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuigong the Turks raided the border again. Changzhi pursued them to Liangjing and suddenly came upon three thousand horsemen still buckling on their armor. Seeing their overconfidence, he charged with two hundred riders and sent them fleeing without their mail.

sentences.zh: 其暮，賊大至，常之潛使人伐木，列炬營中，若烽燧然。

translations.literal: That evening the bandits came in great force; Changzhi secretly had men cut wood and set torches in the camp like beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: That night the enemy arrived in strength. Changzhi secretly had his men cut timber and light torches throughout the camp until it blazed like a chain of signal fires.

sentences.zh: 會風起，賊疑救至，遂夜遁。

translations.literal: When the wind rose, the bandits suspected rescue had arrived and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: A wind sprang up, the enemy took the fires for approaching reinforcements, and stole away in the night.

sentences.zh: 久之，為燕然道大總管，與李多祚王九言等擊突厥骨咄祿、元珍於黃花堆，破之，追奔四十里，賊潰歸磧北。

translations.literal: After a long while he became Grand General of the Yamen circuit; with Li Duozuo, Wang Jiuyan and others he attacked the Turks Gulilu and Yuanzhen at Huanghua mound, defeated them, pursued forty li, and the bandits fled in rout to north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand General of the Yamen circuit. With Li Duozuo, Wang Jiuyan, and others he defeated the Turks Gulilu and Yuanzhen at Huanghua Mound, pursued them forty li, and drove the shattered enemy back across the desert.

sentences.zh: 會左監門衛中郎將爨寶璧欲窮追要功，詔與常之共計，寶壁獨進，為虜所覆，舉軍沒，寶璧下吏誅，常之坐無功。

translations.literal: Then Left Central Imperial Gate Guard Central Brigadier General Nao Baobi wished to pursue to the end for merit; an edict ordered him to plan jointly with Changzhi. Baobi advanced alone and was overrun by the barbarians—the whole army perished. Baobi was imprisoned and executed; Changzhi was punished for no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Left Central Imperial Gate Guard Brigadier Nao Baobi then wanted to chase the rout to the limit for glory. The court ordered him to coordinate with Changzhi, but Baobi pushed ahead alone, was surrounded, and lost his entire force. Baobi was arrested and executed; Changzhi was blamed for accomplishing nothing.

sentences.zh: 會周興等誣其與右鷹揚將軍趙懷節反，捕系詔獄，投繯死。

translations.literal: Then Zhou Xing and others framed him for rebellion with Right Hawk-and-Bow General Zhao Huaijie; he was arrested and imprisoned in the edict prison and died by hanging.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhou Xing and his faction accused him and Right Hawk-and-Bow General Zhao Huaijie of treason. He was thrown into the imperial prison and died on the rope.

sentences.zh: 常之禦下有恩，所乘馬為士所蜺，或請罪之。

translations.literal: Changzhi was gracious to those below; the horse he rode was gnawed by soldiers, and some asked that they be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi treated his men with kindness. Soldiers had chewed on his mount, and some urged that they be punished.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「何遽以私馬鞭官兵乎？

translations.literal: He answered: "Why hasten to whip officers and men over a private horse?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Why flog soldiers over my personal horse?"

sentences.zh: 」前後賞賜分麾下，無留貲。

translations.literal: " Rewards given before and after he divided among his subordinates; he kept no wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever rewards came to him he passed straight to his men and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 及死，人皆哀其枉。

translations.literal: When he died, all mourned his wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, men everywhere grieved that he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 李謹行李謹行，靺鞨人。

translations.literal: Li Jinsheng—Li Jinsheng was a Mohe man.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinsheng was a Mohe tribesman.

sentences.zh: 父突地稽，部酋長也。

translations.literal: His father Tudiji was a tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tudiji had been chief of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 隋末，率其屬千余內附，居營州，授金紫光祿大夫、遼西太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he led over a thousand of his followers to submit inward, dwelling at Yingzhou; he was given the title Grand Master for Golden Purse with Purple Ribbon and Governor of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Sui he brought more than a thousand followers across the border to settle at Yingzhou and was made Grand Master for Golden Purse with Purple Ribbon and Governor of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 武德初，奉朝貢，以其部為燕州，授總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he offered court tribute; his tribe was made Yanzhou and he was appointed commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he began paying tribute to the court; his people were organized as Yanzhou and he was named its commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥叛，突地稽身到定州，上書秦王，請節度。

translations.literal: When Liu Heidao rebelled, Tudiji went in person to Dingzhou and memorialized the Prince of Qin, requesting command authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heidao rose in rebellion, Tudiji went himself to Dingzhou and asked the Prince of Qin for a commission.

sentences.zh: 以戰功封耆國公，徙部居昌平。

translations.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Qi and his tribe was moved to dwell at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: For his victories he was created Duke of Qi, and his tribe was resettled at Changping.

sentences.zh: 高開道以突厥兵攻幽州，突地稽邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao with Turkic troops attacked Youzhou; Tudiji intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Kaidao attacked Youzhou with Turkic allies, Tudiji ambushed and routed him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，進右衛將軍，賜氏李，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was promoted to Right Guard General, granted the surname Li, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was promoted to Right Guard General, given the surname Li, and died.

sentences.zh: 謹行偉容貌，勇蓋軍中，累遷營州都督，家童至數千，以財自雄，夷人畏之。

translations.literal: Jinsheng had an imposing appearance; his courage surpassed all in the army. He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Yingzhou; his household slaves reached thousands; he towered over others by wealth; the barbarians feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsheng was striking in bearing and the bravest man in the army. He rose to Governor of Yingzhou, kept thousands of household slaves, flaunted his wealth, and was feared by the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 為積石道經略大使，論欽陵眾十萬寇湟中，候邏不知，士樵采半散。

translations.literal: As Pacification Commissioner of the Jishi circuit, Lun Qinling led a host of one hundred thousand to raid Huangzhong; border scouts did not know; half the men were scattered gathering firewood.
translations.idiomatic: As Pacification Commissioner of the Jishi route, he faced Lun Qinling, who invaded Huangzhong with a hundred thousand men while the scouts slept. Half his troops were away foraging firewood.

sentences.zh: 謹行聞虜至，即植旗伐鼓，開門以伺。

translations.literal: When Jinsheng heard the barbarians had arrived he immediately planted banners and beat drums, opening the gate to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Jinsheng learned the enemy was near, he raised banners, beat the drums, and threw open the gates as if ready to sally forth.

sentences.zh: 欽陵疑有伏，不敢進。

translations.literal: Qinling suspected an ambush and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qinling suspected a trap and would not come closer.

sentences.zh: 上元三年，破吐蕃於青海，璽書勞勉，封燕國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan he defeated Tibet at Qinghai; an imperial seal letter praised him; he was enfeoffed Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shangyuan he defeated the Tibetans at Qinghai. The emperor sent a sealed letter of praise and created him Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州都督，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Governor of Youzhou and buried at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Youzhou, with burial at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 泉男生泉男生，字元德，高麗蓋蘇文子也。

translations.literal: Ch'eon Namseng—Ch'eon Namseng, style name Yuande, was the son of Goguryeo's Gaisuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Ch'eon Namseng, courtesy name Yuande, was a son of the Goguryeo regent Yeon Gaesomun.

sentences.zh: 九歲，以父任為先人。

translations.literal: At nine years he was made First Attendant through his father's appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he entered office as First Attendant through his father's influence.

sentences.zh: 遷中裏小兄，猶唐謁者也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Middle Palace Junior Brother—like a Tang usher.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Brother of the Middle Palace, a post comparable to a Tang court usher.

sentences.zh: 又為中裏大兄，知國政，凡辭令，皆男生主之。

translations.literal: Again he became Middle Palace Senior Brother, knowing state affairs; all orders and edicts were chiefly managed by Namseng.
translations.idiomatic: He then became Senior Brother of the Middle Palace and took charge of government; Namseng drafted every decree and dispatch.

sentences.zh: 進中裏位頭大兄。

translations.literal: He advanced to Great Brother of the Middle Palace rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Head Great Brother of the Middle Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，為莫離支，兼三軍大將軍，加大莫離支，出按諸部。

translations.literal: After a long while he became Minister, concurrently Great General of the Three Armies; he was given the greater title Great Minister and went forth to inspect all commands.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became Minister and Grand General of the Three Armies, was raised to Great Minister, and toured the provinces on inspection.

sentences.zh: 而弟男建、男產知國事，或曰：「男生惡君等逼己，將除之。

translations.literal: But his younger brothers Namgeon and Namsan handled state affairs. Someone said: "Namseng hates that you press upon him and will eliminate you."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Namgeon and Namsan, however, ran the government at home. Someone warned them, "Namseng resents your pressure on him and means to destroy you."

sentences.zh: 」建、產未之信。

translations.literal: " Namgeon and Namsan did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: They refused to believe it.

sentences.zh: 又有謂男生：「將不納君。

translations.literal: Again someone said to Namseng: "They will not receive you."
translations.idiomatic: Others told Namseng, "They will refuse you entry."

sentences.zh: 」男生遣諜往，男建捕得，即矯高藏命召，男生懼，不敢入。

translations.literal: " Namseng sent a spy; Namgeon captured him and at once counterfeited King Gao Zang's order summoning him. Namseng was afraid and did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Namseng sent a spy; Namgeon seized him and forged an order from King Gao Zang summoning Namseng home. Namseng was terrified and would not go in.

sentences.zh: 男建殺其子獻忠。

translations.literal: Namgeon killed his son Hyeonjung.
translations.idiomatic: Namgeon put his son Hyeonjung to death.

sentences.zh: 男生走保國內城，率其眾與契丹、靺鞨兵內附，遣子獻誠訴諸朝。

translations.literal: Namseng fled to hold the inner citadel of the state, led his multitude with Khitan and Mohe troops to submit inward, and sent his son Hyeonseong to plead at court.
translations.idiomatic: Namseng withdrew into the inner citadel, rallied his followers with Khitan and Mohe allies, and sent his son Hyeonseong to appeal to Tang.

sentences.zh: 高宗拜獻誠右武衛將軍，賜乘輿、馬、瑞錦、寶刀，使還報。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong appointed Hyeonseong General of the Right Martial Guard, gave him imperial carriage, horses, auspicious brocade and treasured sword, and sent him back with word.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong made Hyeonseong General of the Right Martial Guard, gave him an imperial carriage, horses, brocade, and a treasured sword, and sent him back with the court's answer.

sentences.zh: 詔契苾何力率兵援之，男生乃免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qibi Heli to lead troops to rescue him; Namseng was thereby saved.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qibi Heli to march to his relief, and Namseng escaped destruction.

sentences.zh: 授平壤道行軍大總管，兼持節安撫大使，舉哥勿、南蘇、旨巖等城以降。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Pyeongyang circuit campaign army, concurrently holding the staff as Pacification Commissioner; he brought over the cities of Geogeul, Nansu, Juam and others in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Grand General of the Pyongyang campaign and Pacification Commissioner with full powers, and one by one the cities of Geogeul, Nansu, Juam, and others submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 帝又命西臺舍人李虔繹就軍慰勞，賜袍帶、金扣七事。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Palace Gentleman Li Qianyi to go to the army to console and reward; he was given robe, belt, and seven gold fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Palace Gentleman Li Qianyi to the front to console him and bestowed a robe, belt, and seven gold ornaments.

sentences.zh: 明年，召入朝，詔所過州縣傳舍作鼓吹，右羽林將軍李同以飛騎仗廷寵。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to court; an edict ordered postal lodges in every prefecture and county along the way to perform music; Right Forest General Li Tong with the Flying Cavalry guard formed ranks in the courtyard to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to court. Every relay station along the route was ordered to sound drums and pipes, and Right Forest General Li Tong lined the Flying Cavalry in the courtyard to receive him in honor.

sentences.zh: 遷遼東大都督、玄菟郡公，賜第京師。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor-General of Liaodong and Duke of Xuantu commandery; a mansion in the capital was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor-General of Liaodong and Duke of Xuantu, with a mansion granted in the capital.

sentences.zh: 因詔還軍，與李勣攻平壤，使浮屠信誠內間，引高麗銳兵潛入，擒高藏。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered him back to the army; with Li Jiji he attacked Pyongyang; he had the monk Shincheng conduct inner intrigue, drawing Goguryeo elite troops inside secretly, and captured Gao Zang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered back to the field. With Li Jiji he besieged Pyongyang, using the monk Shincheng as an inside agent to lure Goguryeo's best troops within the walls and seize King Gao Zang.

sentences.zh: 詔遣子賫手制、金皿，即遼水勞賜。

translations.literal: An edict sent his son to present the emperor's own writing and gold vessels, immediately at Liaoshui to console and reward.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent his son bearing the emperor's own hand and gold vessels to reward him on the spot at Liaoshui.

sentences.zh: 還，進右衛大將軍、卞國公，賜寶器、宮侍女二、馬八十。

translations.literal: On return he was promoted to Great General of the Right Guard, Duke of Bian; he was given precious vessels, two palace serving women, and eighty horses.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Great General of the Right Guard and Duke of Bian, and received precious vessels, two palace women, and eighty horses.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，詔安撫遼東，並置州縣，招流冗，平斂賦，罷力役，民悅其寬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng an edict ordered him to pacify Liaodong, establish prefectures and counties, summon displaced persons, level and collect taxes, cease corvée labor; the people were pleased with his leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yifeng he was charged with pacifying Liaodong, setting up prefectures and counties, resettling refugees, easing taxes, and ending forced labor. The people welcomed his moderation.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六，帝為舉哀，贈并州大都督。

translations.literal: He died, age forty-six; the emperor mourned for him; posthumously made Governor-General of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six. The emperor mourned him personally and posthumously made him Governor-General of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪至都，詔五品以上官哭之，謚曰襄，勒碑著功。

translations.literal: When the funeral reached the capital, an edict ordered fifth-rank and above officials to weep for him; posthumous name Xiang; a stele was carved recording his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the bier reached the capital, officials of the fifth rank and above were ordered to attend the mourning. He was given the posthumous name Xiang, and a stele was erected to record his deeds.

sentences.zh: 男生純厚有禮，奏對敏辯，善射藝。

translations.literal: Namseng was pure, generous and courteous; in memorial responses he was quick and eloquent; skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Namseng was sincere, courteous, and quick-witted in audience, and a fine archer.

sentences.zh: 其初至，伏斧锧待罪，帝宥之，世以此稱焉。

translations.literal: When he first arrived he lay prostrate awaiting punishment by axe and halberd; the emperor pardoned him—the world praised this.
translations.idiomatic: On first reaching court he prostrated himself beneath the executioner's axe to await judgment; the emperor pardoned him, and men ever after spoke of it with praise.

sentences.zh: 子獻誠獻誠，天授中以右衛大將軍兼羽林衛。

translations.literal: His son Hyeonseong—Hyeonseong, in the Tianshou era served as Great General of the Right Guard concurrently in the Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hyeonseong served in the Tianshou era as Great General of the Right Guard and also in the Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 武后嘗出金幣，命宰相、南北牙群臣舉善射五輩，中者以賜。

translations.literal: Empress Wu once brought out gold and coins, ordering chancellors and officials of the Southern and Northern Gates to nominate five groups of skilled archers; those who hit the mark were given rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once put up gold and cash and told the chancellors and courtiers of both gates to name five teams of marksmen; whoever hit the target received the prize.

sentences.zh: 內史張光輔舉獻誠，獻誠讓右玉鈐衛大將軍薛吐摩支，摩支固辭。

translations.literal: Interior Secretary Zhang Guangfu nominated Hyeonseong; Hyeonseong yielded the place to Xue Tumozhi, Great General of the Right Jade Clasp Guard, and Tumozhi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Secretary Zhang Guangfu nominated Hyeonseong, but Hyeonseong recommended Xue Tumozhi, Great General of the Right Jade Clasp Guard, instead; Tumozhi refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 獻成曰：「陛下擇善射者，然皆非華人。

translations.literal: Hyeonseong said: "Your Majesty is choosing skilled archers, yet none are Chinese."
translations.idiomatic: Hyeonseong said, "Your Majesty seeks marksmen, but you have chosen none who are Chinese."

sentences.zh: 臣恐唐官以射為恥，不如罷之。

translations.literal: Your servant fears Tang officials will take archery as shame; better to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Han officials will be shamed by this—better to cancel the contest altogether.

sentences.zh: 」后嘉納。

translations.literal: The empress approved and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣嘗求貨，獻誠不答，乃誣其謀反，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen once sought goods; Hyeonseong did not respond, so he falsely charged him with plotting rebellion and strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen once demanded a bribe; when Hyeonseong refused, Lai fabricated treason charges and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 後後知其冤，贈右羽林衛大將軍，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: Later the empress knew his injustice, posthumously made him Great General of the Right Forest Guard, and reburied him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress later learned of the injustice, she posthumously appointed him Great General of the Right Forest Guard and gave him a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 李多祚李多祚，其先靺鞨酋長，號「黃頭都督」，後入中國，世系湮遠。

translations.literal: Li Duozuo—Li Duozuo: his ancestors were Mohe chieftains, styled "Yellow-Head Commandant"; later they entered China; the lineage was lost in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duozuo came of Mohe chieftains who had been called the "Yellow-Head Commandant" before entering China; by his day the family's distant origins were forgotten.

sentences.zh: 至多祚，驍勇善射，以軍功累遷右鷹揚大將軍。

translations.literal: By Duozuo's time he was fierce and brave and skilled in archery; for military merit he was repeatedly promoted to Great General of the Right Falcon-Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo himself was a fierce warrior and fine archer who rose through repeated promotion, eventually becoming Great General of the Right Falcon-Banner.

sentences.zh: 討黑水靺鞨，誘其渠長，置酒高會，因醉斬之，擊破其眾。

translations.literal: Campaigning against the Blackwater Mohe, he enticed their chieftains, set out wine in a grand feast, and when they were drunk beheaded them, crushing their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Blackwater Mohe he lured their chiefs to a feast, slew them once they were drunk, and routed their tribes.

sentences.zh: 室韋及孫萬榮之叛，多祚與諸將進討，以勞改右羽林大將軍，遂領北門衛兵。

translations.literal: When the Shiwei and Sun Wanrong rebelled, Duozuo marched with the generals to suppress them; for his labors he was transferred to Great General of the Right Forest Guard and then commanded the Northern Gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shiwei and Sun Wanrong rose in rebellion, Duozuo campaigned with other generals to crush them. Rewarded for his exertions with appointment as Great General of the Right Forest Guard, he came to command the Northern Gate garrison.

sentences.zh: 張柬之將誅二張，以多祚素感概，可動以義，乃從容謂曰：「將軍居北門幾何？

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi was about to execute the two Zhangs; because Duozuo was by nature impassioned and could be moved by righteousness, he calmly said to him: "General, how long have you held the Northern Gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi, planning to kill the Zhang brothers, knew Duozuo's fervent temperament and that duty might sway him. He said gently, "General, how many years have you held the Northern Gate?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「三十年矣。

translations.literal: He said: "Thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo answered, "Thirty years."

sentences.zh: 」「將軍擊鐘鼎食，貴重當世，非大帝恩乎？

translations.literal: "General, you strike bells and eat from tripods—you are honored and weighty in the age—is this not the late emperor's grace?"
translations.idiomatic: "You dine to the sound of bells from vessels of state—your rank and wealth are the wonder of the age. Is that not the late emperor's gift?"

sentences.zh: 」多祚泣數行下，曰：「死且不忘！

translations.literal: Duozuo wept several lines down his face and said: "Even in death I shall not forget!"
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo wept freely. "I would die before I forgot that debt!"

sentences.zh: 」柬之曰：「將軍知感恩，則知所以報，今在東宮乃大帝子，而嬖豎擅朝，危逼宗社。

translations.literal: Jianzhi said: "General, knowing gratitude, you know how to repay it. Now in the Eastern Palace is the late emperor's son, yet favored minions monopolize the court and endanger the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi continued, "If you know gratitude, you know how to repay it. The crown prince is the late emperor's own son, yet minions hold the court and threaten the realm."

sentences.zh: 國家廢興在將軍，將軍誠有意乎？

translations.literal: Whether the state rises or falls is in the general's hands—does the general truly have the will?
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's survival rests with you. Will you act?

sentences.zh: 舍今日尚何在？

translations.literal: If not today, then where else?"
translations.idiomatic: If not today, when?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「茍緣王室，惟公所使。

translations.literal: He answered: "If it concerns the royal house, I am at the Duke's command."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If it is for the house of Tang, I am yours to command."

sentences.zh: 乃引天地以自誓，辭氣毅然，柬之遂定謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he invoked Heaven and Earth to swear himself, his words and tone firm; Jianzhi then fixed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: He swore by Heaven and Earth, his voice steady and resolved, and Jianzhi's plan was settled.

sentences.zh: 以敬暉、李湛為右羽林將軍，命總禁兵，與多祚、王同皎請太子至玄武門，斬關入。

translations.literal: He appointed Jing Hui and Li Zhan Right Forest Guard generals, ordered them to command the forbidden troops; with Duozuo and Wang Tongjiao they invited the crown prince to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the barrier and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui and Li Zhan were made generals of the Right Forest Guard and placed over the palace guards. With Duozuo and Wang Tongjiao they brought the crown prince to the Xuanwu Gate, forced the pass, and entered.

sentences.zh: 及長生殿，白武後曰：「諸將誅逆臣易之、昌宗，恐漏大謀，不敢豫奏，頓首請歸死。

translations.literal: At the Hall of Eternal Life they told Empress Wu: "The generals have executed the traitorous ministers Yizhi and Changzong; fearing a leak of the great plot we dared not report beforehand—we kowtow and beg to die for this."
translations.idiomatic: At the Hall of Eternal Life they reported to Empress Wu, "Your generals have executed the traitors Yizhi and Changzong. Lest our plan be betrayed we did not inform you beforehand—we prostrate ourselves and beg for death."

sentences.zh: 」後病臥，顧湛曰：「我於而父子不薄，亦豫是邪？

translations.literal: The empress, ill in bed, turned to Zhan and said: "I was not stingy to you father and son—were you too part of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress, lying ill, turned to Li Zhan and said, "Have I been unkind to your house? Were you in this too?"

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，封多祚遼陽郡王，食實戶八百，子承訓為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored to the throne, Duozuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoyang, with a fief of eight hundred households; his son Cheng Xun was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong was restored, Duozuo was made Prince of Liaoyang with a fief of eight hundred households, and his son Cheng Xun was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs.

sentences.zh: 湛遷大將軍，封趙國公，食實戶五百。

translations.literal: Zhan was transferred to Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao State, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan was promoted to Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 帝祠太廟，特詔多祚與相王登輿夾侍。

translations.literal: When the emperor sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he specially ordered Duozuo and the Prince of Xiang to mount the carriage and attend on either side.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial ancestral temple sacrifice, the emperor specially ordered Duozuo and the Prince of Xiang to ride the imperial carriage and attend him on either side.

sentences.zh: 監察御史王覿謂多祚夷人，雖有功，不宜共輿輦。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wang Di said Duozuo was a barbarian; though he had merit, he ought not share the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Wang Di objected that Duozuo, though meritorious, was a foreigner and should not ride beside the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕推以心腹，卿勿復言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I treat him as my own heart and belly—do not speak of this again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I trust him as I would my own heart—say no more."

sentences.zh: 崔玄暐等得罪，多祚畏禍及，故陽厚韋氏。

translations.literal: When Cui Xuanwei and others were punished, Duozuo feared calamity would reach him, and therefore outwardly treated the Wei clan generously.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Xuanwei and his allies fell from power, Duozuo feared he would be implicated and therefore courted the Wei clan openly.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子誅武三思，多祚與成王千里率兵先至玄武樓下，具言所以誅三思狀，按兵不戰。

translations.literal: When the Stern and Mournful Crown Prince executed Wu Sansi, Duozuo and the Prince of Cheng, Li Qianli, led troops first to the Xuanwu Tower, fully stating the grounds for executing Sansi, and held their forces without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Li Chongjun killed Wu Sansi, Duozuo and Prince Li Qianli of Cheng marched first to the Xuanwu Tower, explained why Sansi had been killed, and held their troops without engaging.

sentences.zh: 宮闈令楊思勖方侍帝，即挺刀斬其婿羽林中郎將野呼利，兵因沮潰，多祚為其下所殺，二子亦見害，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yang Sixu was attending the emperor; he at once drew his blade and slew Duozuo's son-in-law, Central Forest Guard Lieutenant Yehuli; the troops therefore collapsed in defeat; Duozuo was killed by his own men, two sons were also slain, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yang Sixu, attending the emperor, drew his sword and killed Duozuo's son-in-law Yehuli, a lieutenant of the Forest Guard. The army broke and fled; Duozuo was killed by his own troops, two sons perished with him, and his property was seized.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，追復官爵，並宥家屬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and his household was also pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun era his rank and titles were posthumously restored and his family pardoned.

sentences.zh: 李湛湛者，義府最幼子，字興宗，沈厚有度。

translations.literal: Li Zhan—Zhan was Yifu's youngest son, styled Xingzong, deep and measured in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan, the youngest son of Li Yifu, styled Xingzong, was grave, steady, and self-possessed.

sentences.zh: 六歲，授周王府文學，累遷右散騎常侍，襲河間郡公。

translations.literal: At age six he was appointed Literary Scholar of the Prince of Zhou's household; he was repeatedly promoted to Right Regular Attendant, and inherited the title Duke of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was made literary tutor to the Prince of Zhou's household, rose to Right Regular Attendant, and inherited the dukedom of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 武后徙上陽宮，留湛宿衛。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu moved to the Shangyang Palace, Zhan was left on night guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu retired to the Shangyang Palace, Zhan was left to guard her quarters.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復為右散騎常侍，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was again made Right Regular Attendant and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made Right Regular Attendant and granted an iron certificate of immunity.

sentences.zh: 三思惡之，貶果州刺史。

translations.literal: Sansi hated him and had him demoted to prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, who hated him, had him demoted to prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 歷洺、絳二州，累遷左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He served in the two prefectures of Ming and Jiang, and was repeatedly promoted to Great General of the Left Victorious Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ming and Jiang in turn and was eventually promoted to Great General of the Left Victorious Army.

sentences.zh: 開元十年卒，贈幽州都督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan he died; posthumously made Military Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Kaiyuan and was posthumously made military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，義府以立武后故得宰相，而湛為中興功臣，世不以其父惡為貶雲。

translations.literal: At the outset, Yifu became chancellor because he had established Empress Wu, yet Zhan was a meritorious minister of the restoration; the age did not demean him for his father's evil.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yifu had risen to chancellor by helping make Empress Wu, Zhan was honored as a hero of the restoration, and the world did not hold the father's disgrace against the son.

sentences.zh: 論弓仁論弓仁，本吐蕃族也。

translations.literal: Lun Gongren—Lun Gongren was originally of the Tibetan people.
translations.idiomatic: Lun Gongren was a Tibetan by birth.

sentences.zh: 父欽陵，世相其國。

translations.literal: His father Qinling had for generations been chief minister of that state.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinling had for generations served as chief minister of Tibet.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年，弓仁以所統吐渾七千帳自歸，授左玉鈐衛將軍，封酒泉郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenglu, Gongren brought the seven thousand households of Tuyuhun he commanded to submit of his own accord; he was appointed General of the Left Jade Clasp Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenglu he led seven thousand Tuyuhun households to defect to Tang and was made General of the Left Jade Clasp Guard and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 神龍三年，為朔方軍前鋒遊弈使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenlong he became Vanguard Patrol Commissioner of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenlong he was made vanguard patrol commissioner of the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 時張仁願築三受降城，弓仁以兵出諾真水、草心山為邏衛。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Renyuan was building the three Accept-Surrender cities; Gongren led troops out along the Nuozhen River and Caoxin Mountain as border guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Renyuan built the three Accept-Surrender cities, Gongren patrolled the Nuozhen River and Caoxin Mountain with troops to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 開元初，突厥九姓亂，弓仁引軍度漠，逾白檉林，收火拔部喻多真種落，降之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan the nine surnames of the Turks rebelled; Gongren led his army across the desert, crossed the White Tamarisk Forest, gathered the Yuduozhen clans of the Huoba tribe, and brought them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when the nine Turkic tribes rebelled, Gongren crossed the desert and the White Tamarisk Forest, brought in the Yuduozhen clans of the Huoba tribe, and accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 趯跌思太叛，戰赤柳澗，弓仁騎才五百，自新堡進，時賊四環之，眾不敵，弓仁椎牛誓士自若，再宿潰圍出，人服其壯。

translations.literal: Ashide Sita rebelled; they fought at Red Willow Ford. Gongren had only five hundred horsemen and advanced from Xinbao; at the time the rebels surrounded him on four sides and his force could not match them; Gongren slaughtered an ox to swear his men, calm as ever; after two nights he broke the encirclement and got out; men admired his valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashide Sita rebelled, Gongren met him at Red Willow Ford with only five hundred horsemen marching from Xinbao. The enemy surrounded him on every side. He slaughtered an ox to rally his men, remained unshaken, and after two nights broke out of the encirclement. All who heard of it marveled at his courage.

sentences.zh: 凡閱大小戰數百，未嘗負。

translations.literal: In all he underwent several hundred great and small battles and never once lost.
translations.idiomatic: He fought several hundred engagements, large and small, and never once lost.

sentences.zh: 賜寶玉、甲第、良田，等列莫與比。

translations.literal: He was granted precious jades, a fine mansion, and fertile fields; none of his rank could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: He received jade treasures, a grand mansion, and rich farmland—no peer among his peers.

sentences.zh: 累遷左驍衛大將軍、朔方副大使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Great General of the Left Martial Steeds Guard and Deputy Commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Great General of the Left Martial Steeds Guard and deputy commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 會病，玄宗遣上醫馳視。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Xuanzong sent a senior physician posthaste to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Emperor Xuanzong sent his chief physician posthaste to attend him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈撥川郡王，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died, age sixty-six; posthumously made Prince of Bochuan; posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six, was posthumously made Prince of Bochuan, and given the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 孫惟貞孫惟貞。

translations.literal: Sun Weizhen—Sun Weizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Weizhen.

sentences.zh: 惟貞，名瑀，以字行。

translations.literal: Weizhen, personal name Yu, went by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen, whose personal name was Yu, was known by his style.

sentences.zh: 誌向恢大。

translations.literal: His aims and aspirations were broad and great.
translations.idiomatic: His ambitions were large and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 開元末，為左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he was General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyuan he served as general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在靈武，以衛尉少卿募兵綏、銀，閱旬，眾數萬。

translations.literal: When Suzong was at Lingwu, as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs he raised troops in Sui and Yin; within ten days his force numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, he served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Studs and raised troops in Sui and Yin; within ten days he had gathered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 從還鳳翔，遷光祿卿，為元帥前鋒討擊。

translations.literal: He followed the return to Fengxiang, was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Clan, and served as the marshal's vanguard in punitive attacks.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court back to Fengxiang, was made Minister of the Imperial Clan, and led the marshal's vanguard in punitive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 戰陜州，以功進殿中監。

translations.literal: He fought at Shaan Prefecture and, for merit, was advanced to Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Shaan Prefecture and, for his merit, was promoted to palace supervisor.

sentences.zh: 史思明攻李光弼於河陽，周摯以兵二十萬陣城下，惟貞請銳卒數千，鑿數門出，自旦及午，苦戰破之。

translations.literal: Shi Siming attacked Li Guangbi at Heyang; Zhou Zhi arrayed two hundred thousand troops below the city; Weizhen requested several thousand crack soldiers, broke through several gates to sally forth, and from dawn till noon fought bitterly and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming besieged Li Guangbi at Heyang, Zhou Zhi deployed two hundred thousand men below the walls. Weizhen took several thousand elite troops, broke out through multiple gates, and from dawn to noon fought until he routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 光弼表為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Guangbi memorialized to make him Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Opening an Office with the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi memorialized that he be made Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Opening an Office of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 光弼討史朝義，以惟貞守徐州。

translations.literal: When Guangbi campaigned against Shi Chaoyi, he left Weizhen to guard Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi campaigned against Shi Chaoyi, he left Weizhen to hold Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊將謝欽讓據陳，乃假惟貞潁州刺史，斬賊將，降者萬人。

translations.literal: The rebel general Xie Qinrang held Chen; he therefore provisionally made Weizhen prefect of Yingzhou; he beheaded a rebel general and ten thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Xie Qinrang held Chen. Weizhen was given acting appointment as prefect of Ying, beheaded an enemy commander, and accepted the surrender of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 封蕭國公，實封百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao State, with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao with a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 光弼病，表以自代。

translations.literal: When Guangbi fell ill, he memorialized that Weizhen replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi fell ill, he memorialized recommending Weizhen as his successor.

sentences.zh: 擢左領軍衛大將軍，為英武軍使，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Great General of the Left Victorious Army Guard, made commissioner of the Yingwu Army, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to great general of the Left Victorious Army Guard, made commissioner of the Yingwu Army, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 尉遲勝尉遲勝，本王於闐國。

translations.literal: Yuchi Sheng—Yuchi Sheng was originally king of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Sheng had been king of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，入朝，獻名玉、良馬。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he came to court and presented famous jades and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he came to court and presented famed jades and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以宗室女妻之，授右威衛將軍、毘沙府都督。

translations.literal: Xuanzong gave him an imperial clanswoman in marriage and appointed him General of the Right Majestic Guard and Military Governor of Kucha Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong gave him an imperial clanswoman in marriage and appointed him general of the Right Majestic Guard and military governor of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 歸國，與安西節度使高仙芝擊破薩毘、播仙。

translations.literal: Returning to his state, together with Gao Xianzhi, Military Commissioner of Anxi, he defeated Sabi and Boxian.
translations.idiomatic: On returning home he joined Anxi military commissioner Gao Xianzhi in defeating Sabi and Boxian.

sentences.zh: 累進光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，勝使弟曜攝國事，身率兵五千赴難。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Sheng had his younger brother Yao administer state affairs and personally led five thousand troops to answer the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Sheng left his brother Yao to govern Khotan and personally led five thousand men to aid the Tang.

sentences.zh: 國人固留勝，勝以少女為質而行。

translations.literal: His countrymen firmly detained Sheng; Sheng left a young daughter as hostage and departed.
translations.idiomatic: His subjects tried hard to keep him, so he left a young daughter behind as hostage and set out.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉之，拜特進，兼殿中監。

translations.literal: Suzong commended him and appointed him Special Advancement, concurrently Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong praised his loyalty and appointed him special advancement and palace supervisor.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，進驃騎大將軍，遣還，固請留宿衛。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and sent back, but firmly requested to remain on night guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangde era he was promoted to general of agile cavalry and ordered home, but he begged to remain at court on palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 加開府儀同三司，封武都郡王，實封百戶。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Opening an Office with the Third Rank, enfeoffed as Prince of Wudu, with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Opening an Office of the Third Rank, enfeoffed as Prince of Wudu with a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 勝請授國於曜，詔可。

translations.literal: Sheng requested to transfer the state to Yao; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng asked to pass the throne to Yao, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 勝既留，乃穿築池觀，厚賓客，士大夫多從之遊。

translations.literal: Once Sheng had remained, he dug and built pools and pavilions, treated guests generously, and many scholar-officials followed him in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stayed at court, he built pools and pavilions, entertained guests lavishly, and many scholar-officials sought his company.

sentences.zh: 從德宗至興元，為右領軍將軍，歷睦王傅。

translations.literal: He followed Dezong to Xingyuan, was made General of the Right Victorious Army, and served as tutor to the Prince of Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Dezong to Xingyuan, was made general of the Right Victorious Army, and served as tutor to the Prince of Mu.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，曜上言：「國中以嫡承嗣，今勝讓國，請立其子銳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, Yao submitted a memorial: "In our state the legitimate heir succeeds; now Sheng has yielded the state—please establish his son Rui."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, Yao memorialized, "Succession in our kingdom follows the legitimate line. Since Sheng has yielded the throne, please install his son Rui."

sentences.zh: 」帝欲遣銳襲王。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to send Rui to inherit the kingship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to send Rui to succeed as king.

sentences.zh: 勝固辭，以「曜久行國事，人安之；

translations.literal: Sheng firmly declined, saying: "Yao has long administered state affairs and the people are at ease with him;"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng firmly objected: "Yao has governed for years and the people are content with him;"

sentences.zh: 銳生京華，不習其俗，不可遣」。

translations.literal: "Rui was born in the capital and does not know their customs—he must not be sent."
translations.idiomatic: "Rui was born at court and does not know Khotan's ways—he must not be sent."

sentences.zh: 當是時，兄弟讓國，人莫不賢之。

translations.literal: At that time, brothers yielding the state—no one failed to esteem them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, men everywhere praised the brothers for yielding the throne to one another.

sentences.zh: 睦府除，徙原王傅。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Mu's household was abolished, he was transferred to tutor of the Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the household of the Prince of Mu was abolished, he was made tutor to the Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涼州都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Military Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made military governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尚可孤尚可孤，字可孤，東部鮮卑宇文之別種，世處松、漠間。

translations.literal: Shang Kejiu—Shang Kejiu, styled Kejiu, was a separate branch of the Eastern Xianbei Yuwen, for generations dwelling between Songmo and the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Kejiu, styled Kejiu, was a branch of the Eastern Xianbei Yuwen clan who had long lived between Songmo and the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，隸范陽節度使安祿山，復事史思明。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was attached to An Lushan, Military Commissioner of Fanyang, and later served Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao he served under Fanyang military commissioner An Lushan, and later under Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 上元中，自賊所歸，累授左、右威衛大將軍，封白水縣伯，為神策大將。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he returned from the rebels; he was repeatedly appointed Great General of the Left and Right Majestic Guards, enfeoffed as Earl of Baishui, and made a general of the Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era he defected from the rebels, was repeatedly made great general of the Left and Right Majestic Guards, enfeoffed as Earl of Baishui, and appointed a general of the Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 以功試太常卿。

translations.literal: For merit he was provisionally made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was given acting appointment as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 徙封馮翊郡王，食寶戶一百五十。

translations.literal: He was transferred to enfeoffment as Prince of Fengyi, with a fief of one hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prince of Fengyi with a fief of one hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩主衛兵，器其勇，養為子，名智德。

translations.literal: Yu Chaoen commanded the guard troops, admired his valor, adopted him as a son, and named him Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen, who commanded the palace guards, admired his courage, adopted him as a son, and named him Zhide.

sentences.zh: 使將兵三千，屯扶風、武功，歷十余年，隊伍閑整。

translations.literal: He was sent to command three thousand troops garrisoned at Fufeng and Wugong; over more than ten years his ranks were orderly and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: He was given command of three thousand men garrisoned at Fufeng and Wugong; for more than ten years his troops remained disciplined and well ordered.

sentences.zh: 朝恩死，詔賜氏李，名嘉勛。

translations.literal: When Chaoen died, an edict granted him the surname Li and the name Jiaxun.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoen's death, an edict granted him the surname Li and the name Jiaxun.

sentences.zh: 李希烈叛，擢為招討，應援荊襄，使復本姓名，累戰有功。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, he was promoted to punitive commissioner, sent to reinforce Jing and Xiang, ordered to resume his original surname and name, and repeatedly fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, he was made punitive commissioner to reinforce Jing and Xiang, restored to his original name Shang Kejiu, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之難，召可孤，可孤率兵三千，道襄、鄧而西，屬賊兵銳，乃壁七盤。

translations.literal: In the crisis of Zhu Ci, Kejiu was summoned; Kejiu led three thousand troops west by way of Xiang and Deng; as the rebel troops were sharp, he fortified at Qipan.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion he was summoned to court. He led three thousand men west through Xiang and Deng, but finding the rebels strong, he fortified at Qipan.

sentences.zh: 偽將仇敬忠等來寇，可孤擊卻之，遂收藍田。

translations.literal: The false general Qiu Jingzhong and others came to attack; Kejiu struck and drove them back, then recovered Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals Qiu Jingzhong and others attacked; Kejiu repulsed them and recovered Lantian.

sentences.zh: 德宗將遷梁州，命引兵守灞上，拜神策、京畿、渭南、商州節度招討使。

translations.literal: When Dezong was about to move to Liangzhou, he ordered him to lead troops to guard Bashang and appointed him punitive commissioner of the Divine Strategy Army, the Capital Region, Weinan, and Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong prepared to withdraw to Liangzhou, he ordered Kejiu to hold Bashang and appointed him punitive commissioner over the Divine Strategy Army, the capital region, Weinan, and Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬忠拒戰，可孤急擊斬之。

translations.literal: Jingzhong resisted battle; Kejiu pressed the attack swiftly and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong gave battle; Kejiu pressed the attack and slew him.

sentences.zh: 進軍與李晟收長安，為先鋒。

translations.literal: Advancing with Li Sheng he recovered Chang'an, serving as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Li Sheng to retake Chang'an and led the van.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校尚書右僕射，封馮翊郡王，食實戶二百。

translations.literal: For his merit he was further made acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyi Commandery, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, created Prince of Fengyi, and granted a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又會諸軍進討李懷光，次沙苑，卒於軍，贈司空。

translations.literal: He again joined the armies in advancing against Li Huaiguang, halted at Shayuan, and died in camp; he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the combined armies against Li Huaiguang, encamped at Shayuan, and died in the field; the court posthumously made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 可孤性謹審沈壯，既有勛勞，未嘗自論功，禦眾公嚴，晟數稱之。

translations.literal: Kejiu was by nature cautious, steady, and grave; though he had merit and toil, he never spoke of his achievements himself, governed the masses with public strictness, and Sheng repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu was cautious, steady, and reserved. Despite his achievements he never boasted of them, ruled his men with impartial severity, and Li Sheng often spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 裴玢裴玢，五世祖糾，本王疏勒，武德中來朝，拜鷹揚大將軍，封天山郡公，留不去，遂籍京兆。

translations.literal: Pei Fen—his fifth-generation ancestor Jiu was originally king of Shule; in Wude he came to court, was appointed General of the Soaring Hawk, enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshan Commandery, remained and did not leave, and thus was registered in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Fen was descended from Jiu, fifth-generation forebear and king of Shule. In the Wude era he came to court, was made General of the Soaring Hawk and Duke of Tianshan, stayed in China, and was registered as a resident of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 玢初事金吾將軍論惟明為傔力。

translations.literal: Fen at first served General of the Golden Guards Lun Weiming as a personal attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fen began as a personal attendant to Lun Weiming, General of the Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，以功封忠義郡王。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, for merit he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While Dezong was besieged at Fengtian, Fen earned the title Prince of Zhongyi for his service.

sentences.zh: 從惟明鎮鄜坊，署牙將。

translations.literal: He followed Weiming in garrisoning Bin and Fang and was appointed a guards officer.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Weiming to the Bin-Fang command and was made a guards officer.

sentences.zh: 後節度使王棲曜卒，中軍將何朝宗夜縱火作亂，玢獨匿不出。

translations.literal: Later, when Military Commissioner Wang Qiyao died, Central Army General He Chaozong set fires by night and raised a revolt; Fen alone hid himself and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When Military Commissioner Wang Qiyao died, Central Army General He Chaozong burned the camp by night and rebelled. Fen alone kept out of sight.

sentences.zh: 遲明，擒朝宗以待命。

translations.literal: At dawn he seized Chaozong and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he seized Chaozong and held him for the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 有詔並軍司馬崔輅斬之，以同州刺史劉公濟領節度，擢玢為司馬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Army Vice Director Cui Luo to execute him jointly; Liu Gongji of Tong Prefecture took command of the circuit, and Fen was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Vice Director Cui Luo to execute Chaozong. Liu Gongji of Tongzhou took over the command, and Fen was promoted to army vice director.

sentences.zh: 逾年，公濟卒，乃授玢節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a year Gongji died, and Fen was then appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Gongji died, and Fen was appointed military commissioner in his place.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，徙山南西道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe he was transferred to the Western Mountain-South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year two he was transferred to the Western Mountain-South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 玢為治嚴棱，畏遠權勢，不務貢奉。

translations.literal: Fen governed with stern severity, feared and kept distant from powerful interests, and did not pursue tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Fen ruled with austere rigor, kept his distance from the powerful, and refused to court favor with lavish tribute.

sentences.zh: 蔬食弊衣，居處取避風雨而已。

translations.literal: He ate plain food and wore worn clothes; his dwelling was only enough to keep off wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on vegetables and worn garments, and his house was no more than shelter from the weather.

sentences.zh: 倉庫完實，百姓安之，當世將帥未有及者。

translations.literal: The granaries were full and solid, the common people were at peace, and among the generals of the age none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His granaries were full, the people were secure, and no commander of his day could equal him.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭位。

translations.literal: He resigned his post on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 入朝，不事騶仗。

translations.literal: Entering court, he did not use an escort of outriders.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court he traveled without an escort of mounted attendants.

sentences.zh: 妻乘竹輿，二侍婢，黃碧縑服。

translations.literal: His wife rode a bamboo litter with two serving maids, dressed in yellow-green plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: His wife rode in a bamboo litter attended by two maids, all dressed in plain yellow-green silk.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，贈尚書左僕射，謚曰節。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and given the posthumous name Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year seven and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with the posthumous name Jie (Integrity).

sentences.zh: 史評贊曰：夷狄性惇固，其能知義所在者，鷙挺不可遷，蓋巧不足而諒常有余。

translations.literal: The historian's appraisal says: The nature of the barbarians is honest and firm; those who can know where righteousness lies stand fierce and upright and cannot be turned aside—perhaps their craft is insufficient, but their good faith is always in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Barbarian peoples are by nature steadfast and sincere. Those among them who grasp where duty lies stand fierce and unbending; they may lack subtlety, but their integrity more than makes up for it.

sentences.zh: 觀大柰等事君，皆一其誌，無有顧望，用能功績光明，為天子倚信。

translations.literal: Observing Danai and the others in serving their lord, all held a single purpose without looking back or hesitating; thereby their achievements shone bright and they became men on whom the Son of Heaven could rely and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Danai and his peers: in serving the throne they held one mind without wavering, and so their deeds shone clear and the emperor could lean on them in full trust.

sentences.zh: 至渾瑊、趯跌、光顏輩，烈垂無窮，惟其諒有余故也。

translations.literal: As for Hun Jian, the Tujue, Li Guangyan, and their kind, their fierce renown extends without end—solely because their good faith was in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Hun Jian, the Tujue chiefs, and Li Guangyan left legacies of valor without end, all because their integrity ran so deep.

sentences.zh: 瑊、光顏自有傳，今類其人著之篇。

translations.literal: Jian and Guangyan have their own biographies; here men of their kind are gathered in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Guangyan have biographies of their own; this chapter collects others of their kind.
